The Basilisk's primary armament is a full-size Mek-scale ER Medium Laser, one of the most powerful energy weapons mounted on any ProtoMek. This weapon allows the Basilisk to inflict considerable damage at ranges normally associated with light BattleMek engagements. An LRM-3 launcher in the main gun mount provides supplementary fire support with two salvos of ammunition, typically used to soften targets at long range before closing to laser range. Five heat sinks manage the substantial thermal output from the ER Medium Laser.

Thirty-eight points of armor make the Basilisk one of the most heavily protected ProtoMeks in service, capable of absorbing multiple medium weapon hits before structural compromise. The trade-off is speed: a forty-five-rated engine provides only forty-three kilometers per hour cruising speed, making the Basilisk slower than an Elemental in powered armor. Without jump jets, the design relies on its heavy armor to survive the approach to engagement range. Most Basilisk operations proceed at a slow, steady pace that contrasts sharply with standard Clan battle doctrine, but the design's exceptional protection allows this conservative approach to succeed where faster but more fragile designs would be destroyed.

The Cecerops is a three-ton second-generation ProtoMek designed by Clan Blood Spirit using resources acquired through collaboration with the Snow Ravens. The first ProtoMek fully designed outside the original Smoke Jaguar program, the Cecerops bears a striking resemblance to the sphinx-raptor found on several Clan worlds, with a snakelike body profile and a forward-thrusting head cowl aerodynamically engineered to reduce drag. Among Blood Spirit ProtoMek forces, piloting a Cecerops is considered an extremely high honor, reflecting both the design's demanding performance envelope and its role as a symbol of the beleaguered Clan's determination to maintain military relevance despite dwindling BattleMek resources.

Speed is the Cecerops' defining characteristic. A forty-five-rated fusion engine drives the three-ton frame to a cruising speed of ninety-seven kilometers per hour with a flank speed approaching one hundred fifty, allowing it to keep pace with most light BattleMeks and hovercraft. Even at rest, the design appears to be in motion; every line of the chassis is optimized for velocity. A single ER Micro Laser provides ammunition-independent firepower, allowing Cecerops Stars to operate for extended periods without resupply, a critical advantage for the resource-strapped Blood Spirits.

When operating in packs, the overwhelming and constant barrage of laser fire from a Cecerops Star can intimidate medium Mek pilots and bring down light Meks with proper tactics. Most Cecerops pilots are highly experienced by the time they earn assignment to the design, and the chaotic swirl of a pack hunting in concert deliberately mimics the sphinx-raptor's predatory behavior. Fourteen points of armor provide reasonable protection for the weight class, though sustained fire from heavier weapons will quickly overwhelm the design's defenses. The Cecerops excels in harassment and pursuit roles where its extraordinary speed can be leveraged without exposing it to concentrated return fire.

The Cecerops was born from an unlikely partnership between Clan Blood Spirit and Clan Snow Raven, two Clans whose shared outsider status in Homeworld politics drove them to collaborate on military technology development. The Snow Ravens provided critical resources and technical assistance that allowed the Blood Spirits to establish their own ProtoMek production capability at the Reserve Industriplex-2 on York. The Cecerops was the first fruit of this collaboration, though it proved an engineering challenge that delayed production until after the smaller and simpler design had already reached the field.

The Cecerops' debut on Arcadia was marred by controversy. Star Colonel Suzanne Church of the 171st Crimson Guards, commanding an entire Trinary of Cecerops and Chrysaors, treated the ProtoMeks as glorified Elementals rather than exploiting their speed and mobility. Predictably, the machines were overkill against enemy Elementals and wasted when deployed in tight terrain with limited maneuver space. When Church blamed the Cecerops for her command's poor showing, a Cecerops pilot named Andre challenged her to a Trial of Grievance. Issued in front of other Star Colonels and her own troops, Church could not refuse without losing honor. Despite fighting augmented, Church fell to Andre's clever tactical exploitation of the Cecerops' capabilities, simultaneously winning the Trial and demonstrating the design's true potential.

With BattleMeks becoming increasingly scarce in the constant warfare for York between the Spirits and Star Adders, ProtoMeks gradually usurped much of the Blood Spirit touman as a necessary weapon of choice. The Cecerops became the prestige assignment among the Clan's ProtoMek forces, with failed MekWarrior sibkos reportedly adapting to the program to maintain the large numbers the Clan needed to field effectively. Several initial shipments went to the Snow Ravens as payment for their assistance, though this arrangement ended in 3071 with the Ravens' abrupt departure from Clanspace.

Production disruptions followed when Clan Cloud Cobra destroyed one of the Blood Spirit production facilities, though the Spirits managed to convert a defunct facility on Albion left behind by the departing Ravens. During the constant clashes with the Star Adders on Arcadia and Albion, several variant configurations were developed to address specific tactical requirements, expanding the Cecerops' role beyond its original pure-speed reconnaissance mission. Contradicting Blood Spirit exclusivity, modified Cecerops were also reportedly sighted among mysterious gray-painted raiding forces that struck targets across the Falcon and Horse Occupation Zones in late 3073, their origin and allegiance unknown.

The Centaur’s defining characteristic is the breadth of its engagement envelope. Its base configuration mounts an LRM-3 launcher for long-range harassment, an SRM-2 rack for close-range punch, and an ER Micro Laser in the main gun mount for point defense, giving a Point of Centaurs the ability to threaten targets from beyond five hundred meters down to knife-fighting range. The forty-five-rated fusion engine drives the five-ton frame to a respectable cruising speed of sixty-five kilometers per hour with a flank speed approaching one hundred, allowing it to keep pace with medium BattleMechs and outrun most heavy designs.

These advantages come at a cost. The Centaur carries only eight LRM salvos and ten SRM reloads in its base configuration, giving a pilot roughly two minutes of sustained missile fire before being reduced to the ER Micro Laser alone. Armor protection is modest at best, with twenty points distributed across the frame; a single large laser hit to the center torso will breach the internal structure. Without jump jets, the Centaur is also vulnerable to being cornered in broken terrain. Commanders typically deploy Centaur Points in fast-moving screening roles where their speed and multi-range firepower can be leveraged without exposing them to the sustained fire that would quickly overwhelm their limited protection.

The Centaur traces its origins to the secret ProtoMech development program undertaken by Clan Smoke Jaguar scientists on Huntress following the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052. Facing severe resource shortages and mounting guerrilla resistance in their Inner Sphere occupation zone, Jaguar scientists conceived of a new class of war machine that could be produced at a fraction of the cost of a BattleMech while still fielding meaningful firepower. The Centaur was designed as a versatile mid-weight entry in the ProtoMech lineup, filling the gap between the lightweight scout designs like the Harpy and Siren and the heavier assault platforms like the Gorgon and Minotaur.

The ProtoMech program remained secret until Khan Lincoln Osis discovered it during the desperate defense of Huntress against Task Force Serpent in 3060. Despite his fury at being kept uninformed, the dire circumstances of the Jaguar Annihilation forced Osis to deploy the untested machines. The Centaur and its sibling designs acquitted themselves well against the surprised Inner Sphere forces in the jungles of Huntress, though they could not prevent the Clan’s ultimate destruction. In the aftermath, multiple Clans raided Huntress to seize ProtoMech technology, and production data for the Centaur was among the most sought-after prizes.

Clan Goliath Scorpion secured the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex itself, while Clan Wolf established a Centaur production line at the Csesztreg Industriplex Epsilon on Csesztreg, and Clan Jade Falcon began manufacturing the design at Factory Zone 5 on Erewhon. Clan Hell’s Horses set up their own line at Industriplex Upsilon on Niles, giving the Centaur one of the broadest production networks of any first-generation ProtoMech. This wide dispersal reflected the design’s reputation as a reliable and adaptable platform that could serve multiple tactical roles with minimal modification.

During the 3060s and into the Jihad era, several variant configurations were developed by different Clans to address specific tactical requirements. Clan Fire Mandrill’s Kindraa Payne-Beyl-Grant produced the close-combat-oriented Centaur 2 at their facility on Shadow, while Clan Snow Raven developed the energy-focused Centaur 3 at the Aeroyard Gargain on Bearclaw. The most radical evolution came with the Centaur 4, produced by Clan Coyote at the Yoma Aerospace Plant on Babylon, which incorporated advanced myomer booster technology for dramatically increased sprint capability.

The Wars of Reaving brought further development when the Society produced the Centaur Z at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex, then under Clan Goliath Scorpion control. Equipped with a Magnetic Clamp System for OmniMech transport, the Z variant reflected the Society’s asymmetric approach to warfare. Following the destruction of the Society, surviving Centaur production lines passed through several ownership changes as Clans were absorbed or annihilated during the Reaving. The Csesztreg facility transferred from Clan Wolf to Clan Hell’s Horses, while the Niles line passed to Clan Stone Lion. Despite the upheaval, the Centaur remains in active production across the Clan Homeworlds, its fundamental design having proven sound enough to justify over six decades of continuous manufacture.

The Chrysaor is a six-ton second-generation ProtoMek jointly developed by Clan Blood Spirit and Clan Snow Raven. Originally intended to be the first product of their ProtoMek collaboration, engineering challenges delayed the Chrysaor's introduction until after the lighter Cecerops had already reached the field. Its first battlefield appearance on Arcadia was controversial, with a Star Colonel's misuse of the design nearly dooming its acceptance among the already-skeptical Blood Spirit warrior caste. Only a dramatic Trial of Grievance by a Chrysaor pilot against the offending commander salvaged the design's reputation and demonstrated its true capabilities.

The Chrysaor is a solid medium-weight ProtoMek built around four ER Micro Lasers distributed across the arms and torso. The all-energy loadout eliminates ammunition dependency, allowing extended operations critical for the resource-constrained Blood Spirits and the far-flung Snow Raven garrisons. A fifty-five-rated engine provides sixty-four kilometers per hour cruising speed with a flank approaching one hundred, sufficient to keep pace with most Meks and ProtoMeks. Twenty-eight points of armor, nearly a ton and a half, provide strong protection against lighter weapons.

At short range, the four ER Micro Lasers can deliver a potent concentrated strike. Combined-arms units that have dispensed with zellbrigen use the Chrysaor to devastating effect: larger units hammer the enemy while a Point of Chrysaors uses their score of laser beams to find the holes in damaged armor and finish targets off, freeing the heavier units to move on to the next engagement. Four heat sinks manage the thermal output from sustained fire, though aggressive pilots who alpha-strike continuously will build heat over time. The Chrysaor excels in the exploitation role, using its speed and sustained-fire capability to capitalize on openings created by heavier forces.

shared: The Delphyne is a nine-ton second-generation ProtoMek developed jointly by Clan Blood Spirit and Clan Fire Mandrill, bearing the aesthetic hallmarks of a dragon in its aggressive visual profile. One of the heaviest standard ProtoMek designs in service, the Delphyne carries firepower sufficient to challenge some Inner Sphere Meks in single combat. The design benefited from lessons learned from the mistakes of the similarly-massed Minotaur, and the Delphyne has rewarded its creators with performance superior to that of its first-generation counterpart across nearly every measurable metric.

The Delphyne's centerpiece is a mouth-mounted Medium Pulse Laser, a weapon system that provides reliable accuracy and solid damage output against targets across a broad range envelope. While not individually terrifying, a full Point of five Delphynes puts five Medium Pulse Lasers on target, easily sufficient to destroy lighter Meks and overwhelm most other ProtoMek designs. A seventy-five-rated fusion engine drives the nine-ton frame to nearly ninety kilometers per hour at flank speed, allowing the Delphyne to pace most Clan heavy Meks and outrun any assault design. Five jump jets provide one hundred fifty meters of leaping distance, giving the heavy design exceptional terrain mobility.

Over two tons of armor at forty-two points provide excellent protection by ProtoMek standards, sufficient to survive even a Gauss rifle hit to the torso without penetrating the internal structure. The all-energy weapons configuration eliminates ammunition dependency entirely, allowing the Delphyne to maintain continuous combat operations without resupply concerns. Four heat sinks manage the Medium Pulse Laser's thermal output effectively. The combination of speed, jump capability, armor protection, and reliable firepower makes the Delphyne one of the most well-rounded ProtoMek designs ever produced, capable of filling multiple tactical roles without significant compromise in any single area.

The Delphyne emerged from the partnership between the Blood Spirits and Fire Mandrills, two Clans whose relatively weak positions in Homeworld politics encouraged cooperation on military technology development. The design was produced at facilities on both Shadow, under Kindraa Payne-Beyl-Grant of the Fire Mandrills, and York under the Blood Spirits. Within the Fire Mandrills, the Delphyne saw regular deployment only among Kindraa Payne-Beyl-Grant's forces, though rare isorla examples occasionally appeared in other Kindraa toumans.

Clan Coyote raids on Foster netted them several dozen Delphynes, many of which were modified and sent out for field-testing with Coyote forces. A major Coyote assault hit Shadow in the first days of 3072, forcing the Delphyne into heavier combat than it had previously experienced. Initial skirmishes against Coyote ProtoMeks went to the invaders, but as the fighting progressed, the Delphyne's lack of ammunition dependency turned the tide against the Coyote Procyons and Rocs, whose missile magazines emptied while the Delphynes maintained continuous fire. Although the Fire Mandrills eventually suffered defeat, it was not the fault of the Delphyne.

Two variants were developed by the original producing Clans. The Delphyne 2 diversified the weapons load with arm-mounted ER Micro Lasers and dual SRM-3 launchers, sacrificing some armor for increased short-range firepower and versatility. The Delphyne 3, labeled as such for tracking purposes, is actually a Coyote modification of captured base-model Delphynes, refitted with an ER Medium Laser and arm-mounted Micro Pulse Laser. These modified machines frequently accompanied Coyote Procyon Points as de facto command ProtoMeks, their heavier firepower providing the punch that the lighter five-ton designs lacked.

Notable among the Delphyne's pilots were Point Commander Kar of the Blood Spirits, one of the first generation raised as ProtoMek pilots, and Warrior Ando of Kindraa Payne-Beyl-Grant, who single-handedly defeated a Mandrill BattleMek through continuous rear-arc fire. Ando was the lone survivor of an isolated engagement against the Coyotes on Shadow, his control system damage leaving him near death and his nervous system overwhelmed. Both pilots exemplified the Delphyne's capacity to produce exceptional results in skilled hands.

The Erinyes is a two-ton second-generation ProtoMek designed by Clan Jade Falcon after obtaining Smoke Jaguar scientific records following the Jaguar Annihilation. Conceived as a proof-of-concept effort to validate the Falcons' ability to independently produce ProtoMek technology, the Erinyes was a deliberately conservative design that hewed closely to the parameters established by the first-generation Harpy. Khan Marthe Pryde terminated the program in 3064 after lackluster performance in test raids against the Lyran Alliance, but the design resurfaced nearly a decade later under mysterious circumstances during devastating attacks on Falcon worlds by unknown forces wielding upgraded Erinyes variants.

Built along similar lines to the Smoke Jaguar Harpy, the Erinyes is barely more than a slightly upgraded battlesuit in practical terms. The base configuration mounts a single SRM-1 launcher in the torso with five rounds of ammunition and four jump jets providing one hundred twenty meters of leaping distance. This gives the Erinyes better terrain mobility than most two-ton designs, though the single missile tube provides woefully inadequate firepower for anything beyond guard duty and riot control. Ten points of armor offer minimal protection against battlefield weapons.

The Erinyes' primary tactical value lies in its jump capability and small profile rather than raw combat power. Operating in Stars or larger formations, Erinyes pilots can use their jump jets to stage ambushes from heavy terrain, concentrating their fire on single targets before fading back into cover along paths too restrictive for pursuing BattleMeks. This hit-and-fade approach proved remarkably effective during the Hellion Incursion, where Falcon Erinyes Points used heavy woodlands and canyon terrain to savage overextended Hellion patrols. However, the design's limited ammunition supply and fragile armor make prolonged engagements untenable.

The Erinyes traces its origins to the Jade Falcon Scientist Caste's earliest efforts to replicate ProtoMek technology acquired from the deceased Smoke Jaguars' records. The design was one of the first ProtoMeks developed outside the original Jaguar program, representing the Falcons' initial foray into a weapon system they had previously shown little interest in. When test raids against Lyran Alliance border worlds in the early 3060s proved disappointing, an unimpressed Khan Marthe Pryde shut down the program, and the existing Erinyes were redistributed to several Periphery border worlds along with their pilots.

The reshuffling that followed, with many front-line units being pulled to the Lyran border after the second Incursion, saw many coreward Falcon worlds garrisoned primarily by solahma units and ProtoMek forces. This left the Falcons ill-prepared when Clan Ice Hellion launched their whirlwind assault along the Falcon's Periphery border in the late 3060s. On Bone Norman, the Hellion 200th Attack Cluster was nearly destroyed thanks to creative ambush tactics by the Falcon Eleventh Provisional Garrison Cluster, whose Trinaries had been partially replaced with Erinyes Points. Star Colonel Vikkers Helmar used the planet's restrictive terrain to devastating effect, sending Erinyes formations to navigate heavy woodlands around the Hellion command post and snipe returning patrols. Working in Stars, the ProtoMeks concentrated their fire on single targets, often crippling them within a few salvos before fading into underbrush along paths too narrow for pursuing BattleMeks.

Despite the official program cancellation, dark rumors persisted in the Periphery that the Falcon Scientist Caste had continued the project at a secret location. These rumors took on alarming substance after devastating attacks on Somerset and Winfield in mid-3072 by an unknown force fielding large numbers of light ProtoMeks, including newly upgraded Erinyes variants. Falcon Watch reports intercepted by Lyran Loki agents revealed the Falcons were in major confusion over the identity and allegiance of their attackers. Popular conjecture among Clan experts attributed the ProtoMeks to the Dark Caste, though the Falcons remained tight-lipped regarding these mysterious incursions across their Occupation Zone between 3072 and 3074.

The attacks also raised troubling questions about the provenance of the newer Erinyes variants detected during this period. The upgraded models sported different engine configurations, weapon loadouts, and armor distributions that suggested ongoing development well beyond what the original Falcon program had achieved before its cancellation. Whether these represented continued secret Falcon development, Dark Caste innovation, or something else entirely remains one of the unresolved mysteries of the Jihad era in the Falcon Occupation Zone.

The Gorgon is an eight-ton first-generation ProtoMek developed by Clan Smoke Jaguar as a heavy fire support platform within the original ProtoMek program on Huntress. Anchoring the heavier end of the ProtoMek weight spectrum alongside the nine-ton Minotaur, the Gorgon is built around a ten-tube LRM launcher that gives it bombardment capability unprecedented for a unit of its size. The LRM-10 is so large relative to the ProtoMek chassis that Jaguar scientists developed the main gun mount specifically to accommodate it, creating a hand-supported weapon system anchored to the torso that became standard on several subsequent ProtoMek designs. The Gorgon served as the long-range anchor of mixed ProtoMek formations, delivering indirect fire support that could suppress or destroy targets well beyond the engagement range of lighter designs.

The Gorgon defining feature is its LRM-10 launcher, a weapon system that would be respectable on a medium BattleMek and is extraordinary on an eight-ton ProtoMek. The ten-missile salvo can deliver withering fire at ranges exceeding six hundred meters, allowing the Gorgon to engage targets that cannot effectively return fire against the small ProtoMek profile at that distance. An ER Micro Laser in the main gun mount provides minimal close-range backup. The fifty-rated fusion engine delivers forty-three kilometers per hour cruising speed with no jump capability, adequate for keeping pace with heavier formations but insufficient for rapid repositioning.

The Gorgon most critical vulnerability is ammunition dependency. The LRM-10 carries only twelve salvos of ammunition, exhausting in less than three minutes of sustained fire. Once the missiles are depleted, the Gorgon is reduced to its ER Micro Laser, a weapon so small that it poses no meaningful threat to anything larger than conventional infantry. Thirty-four points of armor provide decent protection, but the Gorgon lack of speed or jump capability means it cannot easily disengage when its ammunition runs dry. Prudent commanders maintain strict fire discipline in Gorgon Points, parceling out salvos to extend engagement time and planning withdrawal routes before the first missile is launched.

The Gorgon was designed to give ProtoMek formations organic long-range fire support, a capability that the lighter designs in the Smoke Jaguar program could not provide. Jaguar scientists recognized that ProtoMek Points operating without indirect fire support would be forced to close with enemies at ranges where the small machines thin armor became a critical liability. The Gorgon LRM-10 allowed a mixed Point to engage targets at distance, softening them before the lighter ProtoMeks closed to deliver finishing blows. The development of the main gun mount to accommodate the oversized launcher was a significant engineering achievement that influenced all subsequent heavy ProtoMek designs.

At the Battle of Huntress in 3060, Gorgon Points proved devastating against Task Force Serpent forces in several engagements. Operating from concealed positions in the Huntress highlands, Gorgon ProtoMeks delivered LRM fire into Inner Sphere formations that struggled to locate the small launchers at long range. The combination of ProtoMek-sized targets and BattleMek-scale missile fire created tactical problems that Serpent commanders had never trained to address, and several advances were stalled by Gorgon bombardment until the ProtoMeks exhausted their ammunition.

Following the Jaguar Annihilation, the Gorgon attracted particular interest from Clan Snow Raven, which established a production line at the Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on Dante. The Ravens valued the Gorgon long-range fire support capability for defending their scattered naval installations against ground assault. Clan Goliath Scorpion maintained production at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress, while several other Clans acquired limited production capability.

Variant development has explored alternatives to the ammunition-dependent LRM configuration. The Gorgon 2 mounts a Medium Pulse Laser with four jump jets, converting the design from fire support to mobile direct combat. The Gorgon 3 carries dual SRM-4 launchers with an upgraded engine for close-range saturation fire. The Gorgon 4 combines an AP Gauss Rifle with an SRM-6 and jump jets for a versatile multi-role configuration. The Gorgon 5 mounts a Streak LRM-5 and Magnetic Clamp System, while the Gorgon 6 carries an AP Gauss Rifle, Angel ECM Suite, and Myomer Booster for electronic warfare operations.

The Wars of Reaving disrupted Gorgon production at several facilities, but the design broad manufacturing base ensured continuity. The Gorgon remains a critical component of Homeworld Clan ProtoMek formations, its long-range fire support capability proving difficult to replicate in lighter designs. Newer variants have expanded the chassis into roles far beyond its original fire support mandate, demonstrating the fundamental soundness of the eight-ton platform.

The Harpy is a two-ton first-generation ProtoMek developed by Clan Smoke Jaguar as part of the original ProtoMek program on Huntress. The lightest design to emerge from the program, the Harpy blurs the line between battle armor and true combat walker, standing barely taller than an Elemental in powered armor. Despite its diminutive stature, the Harpy mounts a ballistic weapon and three jump jets that grant it remarkable tactical agility for its weight class. Intended primarily for anti-infantry operations and close-range ambush tactics, the Harpy relies on its small profile and jumping ability rather than armor protection or raw firepower to survive on the battlefield.

The Harpy is defined by its jump capability. Three jump jets give the tiny machine ninety meters of leaping distance, allowing it to exploit terrain features that would block larger units and execute flanking maneuvers that heavier ProtoMeks cannot replicate. A single machine gun provides adequate firepower against infantry and battle armor formations, though it struggles to threaten anything with significant armor protection. The ten-rated fusion engine drives the two-ton frame at a modest thirty-two kilometers per hour cruising speed, making the Harpy one of the slower designs when earthbound.

The Harpy carries eleven points of armor, sufficient to absorb a medium laser hit to the torso but offering little margin against sustained fire. In standard battlefield exercises against Elemental battle armor, the Harpy generally fared poorly in direct engagements, as Elementals carry comparable firepower with better anti-Mek capability. The Harpy finds its niche in roles where its larger size offers a psychological advantage over conventional infantry and where its jump jets allow it to control engagement range. Commanders who attempt to use Harpy Points as frontline assault units quickly discover the design limitations, while those who employ them as mobile skirmishers and ambush elements find them surprisingly effective.

The Harpy holds the distinction of being the first ProtoMek design attempted by Clan Smoke Jaguar scientists on Huntress. Conceived in the aftermath of the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052, the ProtoMek program sought to create a class of combat machine that could be manufactured at a fraction of the cost of a BattleMek while requiring pilots smaller than Elemental phenotypes. The Harpy, as the initial proof-of-concept design, was deliberately kept simple and light, allowing scientists to validate the fundamental ProtoMek technologies before scaling up to heavier designs like the Centaur and Minotaur.

The ProtoMek program remained hidden from the Jaguar Khans until the desperate defense of Huntress against Task Force Serpent in 3060. When Khan Lincoln Osis discovered the secret project, the dire circumstances of the Clan Annihilation forced him to deploy the untested machines. The Harpy and its sibling designs saw their combat debut in the jungles of Huntress, where the small ProtoMeks used the dense vegetation and broken terrain to stage ambushes against the surprised Inner Sphere forces. The Harpy proved particularly effective in these conditions, its jump jets allowing it to navigate the canopy gaps and ravines that channeled heavier units into kill zones.

Following the destruction of Clan Smoke Jaguar, multiple Clans raided Huntress to seize ProtoMek production data. The Harpy was among the least coveted designs due to its limited combat capability, but its simplicity made it one of the easiest to reproduce. Clan Coyote and Clan Blood Spirit were the first to establish independent Harpy production, valuing the design as a training platform for ProtoMek pilots and as a low-cost garrison unit. Clan Jade Falcon also acquired Harpy production data but showed little enthusiasm for the design, considering it beneath their martial standards.

The 3060s saw modest variant development as different Clans experimented with the Harpy chassis. The Harpy 2, which replaces the machine gun with an ER Micro Laser, emerged from Clan Wolf efforts to create an ammunition-independent version suitable for extended patrols. The Harpy 3 traded the jump jets for a larger engine and faster ground speed, reflecting Clan Snow Raven preferences for rapid reconnaissance over terrain agility. The Harpy 4 incorporated myomer booster technology for enhanced sprint capability while retaining the original jump configuration.

The Wars of Reaving took a heavy toll on Harpy production capacity as several manufacturing Clans were destroyed or absorbed. Despite this, the Harpy endures as a training and garrison design across the Homeworld Clans. Its low manufacturing cost and simple maintenance requirements ensure continued production even as more capable second-generation designs have largely supplanted it in frontline service. The Harpy remains most commonly encountered in solahma garrison clusters and ProtoMek training cadres, where its forgiving handling characteristics make it an ideal introduction to ProtoMek operations.

The Hydra is a six-ton first-generation ProtoMek designed by Clan Smoke Jaguar as a medium assault platform within the original ProtoMek program on Huntress. Occupying the weight class between the versatile five-ton Centaur and the heavier Roc, the Hydra centers its firepower around a Streak SRM-3 launcher backed by a Micro Pulse Laser, giving it significant hitting power at short to medium range. The design lacks jump capability and carries moderate armor, trading mobility for raw combat effectiveness. In the combined-arms ProtoMek doctrine developed by the Jaguars, the Hydra was intended to serve as the primary engagement platform, closing with enemies identified by lighter scouts and delivering concentrated missile and energy fire.

The Hydra firepower is concentrated in its torso-mounted Streak SRM-3 launcher, which ensures that missiles only fire when the targeting system achieves a solid lock, eliminating waste from near-misses. The three-missile salvo delivers enough kinetic energy to threaten light BattleMek armor, and a full Point of Hydras firing in concert can strip armor from medium-weight targets with alarming efficiency. The Micro Pulse Laser mounted in the main gun provides accurate close-range backup fire, its pulse-firing mode partially compensating for the inherent targeting limitations of the ProtoMek fire control system.

The Hydra most significant limitation is its lack of mobility options. With a cruising speed of only forty-three kilometers per hour and no jump jets, the six-ton design cannot disengage from unfavorable encounters or navigate broken terrain with any agility. Twenty-nine points of armor provide reasonable protection for the weight class but cannot withstand concentrated fire from BattleMek-scale weapons for long. Ammunition dependency is also a concern, as the Streak launcher carries only twelve rounds before being reduced to the Micro Pulse Laser alone. Commanders typically deploy Hydra Points in terrain that favors short-range engagement, where the Streak missiles and pulse laser can be brought to bear before faster enemies can exploit the Hydra limited speed.

The Hydra was developed as the dedicated medium assault ProtoMek in the original Smoke Jaguar lineup, filling the gap between the multi-role Centaur and the heavier fire support designs. Jaguar scientists designed it around the Streak SRM system, recognizing that missile accuracy was critical for a platform too small to carry large ammunition reserves. The combination of Streak technology with a pulse laser created a ProtoMek that could reliably hit its targets at combat ranges where larger machines often struggled against the small, fast-moving ProtoMek profile.

During the Battle of Huntress in 3060, the Hydra proved one of the more effective ProtoMek designs in direct combat. Several Points of Hydras engaged Inner Sphere light and medium BattleMeks at close range in the dense jungle terrain surrounding the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex, using the vegetation to close to optimal missile range before the larger machines could bring their superior firepower to bear. The Streak system proved particularly valuable in the jungle fighting, where standard missiles would have been wasted on deflection shots through heavy foliage.

Following the Jaguar Annihilation, the Hydra attracted interest from Clans that valued direct combat capability over reconnaissance or fire support. Clan Blood Spirit was among the first to establish independent Hydra production, appreciating the design straightforward combat philosophy that aligned with their aggressive martial tradition. Clan Hell Horses also produced the Hydra in significant numbers at Industriplex Upsilon on Niles, integrating it into their combined-arms formations alongside conventional armor and infantry.

Variant development for the Hydra has explored diverse tactical niches. The Hydra 2 mounts a Streak SRM-5 with three jump jets, creating a more mobile but lightly armored missile platform. The Hydra 3 replaces the missile and laser combination with an LRM-6 launcher and jump jets, converting the design into a mobile fire support unit. The Hydra 4 mounts three AP Gauss Rifles, a radical departure that transforms the Hydra into a dedicated anti-battle-armor and anti-infantry platform with exceptional sustained firepower.

The Wars of Reaving disrupted multiple Hydra production lines as the Homeworld Clans turned on each other. Clan Blood Spirit, one of the primary producers, was annihilated during the Reaving, and their production facilities were seized or destroyed. Despite these losses, the Hydra remains in production at several surviving facilities, its reliable combat performance ensuring continued demand among Clans that maintain large ProtoMek formations in their toumans.

The Minotaur is a nine-ton first-generation ProtoMek developed by Clan Smoke Jaguar as the heaviest and most powerful design in the original ProtoMek program on Huntress. Built to serve as the assault element of ProtoMek formations, the Minotaur sacrifices speed for devastating firepower and thick armor protection, mounting two ER Medium Lasers that deliver as much damage as many light BattleMeks. Combined with thirty-six points of armor sufficient to withstand a heavy autocannon hit, the Minotaur represented the upper limit of what first-generation ProtoMek technology could achieve. Its intended role as a defensive strongpoint leverages its impressive combat power while minimizing the impact of its slow ground speed.

The Minotaur twin ER Medium Lasers give it the most potent energy weapon suite of any first-generation ProtoMek, delivering a combined damage output that can threaten medium-weight BattleMeks at respectable range. As energy-only armament, the weapons have no ammunition dependency, allowing the Minotaur to fight indefinitely without resupply. Three jump jets provide ninety meters of jumping distance, partially compensating for the design slow thirty-two-kilometer-per-hour cruising speed. Thirty-six points of armor make the Minotaur the most heavily protected first-generation ProtoMek, capable of surviving hits that would destroy lighter designs outright.

The Minotaur primary weakness is its glacial ground speed. At thirty-two kilometers per hour, it is easily outpaced by virtually every combat unit on the battlefield, including most assault-class BattleMeks. The jump jets help somewhat, but ninety meters of leaping distance is barely adequate for clearing terrain obstacles. An entire Point of Minotaurs working together can concentrate enough firepower to rapidly destroy light and medium targets, but getting into effective range against mobile opponents requires careful positioning and terrain exploitation. The design is at its best in defensive operations where it can select strong positions and force enemies to come to it, leveraging its firepower and armor from prepared fighting positions.

The Minotaur was developed as the capstone of the original Smoke Jaguar ProtoMek program, representing the maximum weight and combat power that first-generation ProtoMek technology could support. Jaguar scientists designed it specifically for the defensive role, recognizing that the ProtoMek concept was best suited to creating multiple small, lethal defensive positions rather than attempting to match BattleMeks in open maneuver warfare. The decision to mount two ER Medium Lasers was considered ambitious for the weight class, but testing proved that the nine-ton chassis could handle the thermal load with proper heat sink integration.

During the Battle of Huntress in 3060, Minotaur Points served as the backbone of Jaguar defensive positions around key installations. Their ability to absorb significant punishment while delivering devastating return fire made them the most feared ProtoMek design among Task Force Serpent personnel. Several Inner Sphere light Mek pilots reported being caught by surprise when what appeared to be a trivially small target returned fire with medium laser energy that could penetrate their armor in two or three exchanges. The Minotaur combination of small size and BattleMek-grade firepower represented a genuinely new tactical challenge.

After the Jaguar Annihilation, the Minotaur became one of the most widely produced ProtoMek designs. Clan Wolf established an early production line at Csesztreg Industriplex Epsilon, while Clan Hell Horses produced Minotaurs at Industriplex Upsilon on Niles. The design straightforward combat philosophy appealed to Clans across the political spectrum, from the aggressive Blood Spirits to the more cautious Diamond Sharks. The Minotaur lack of specialized equipment meant it could be manufactured more easily than probe or ECM-equipped designs.

The Minotaur has inspired the broadest range of variants of any first-generation ProtoMek, reflecting the diverse tactical philosophies of its many operators. The Minotaur 2 mounts an LB-X AC/2 for long-range cluster fire. The Minotaur 3 carries an LRM-12 with jump jets and a faster engine for mobile fire support. The Minotaur 4 mounts a ProtoMek AC/2 with enhanced mobility. The Minotaur P2, from Clan Goliath Scorpion, adds a Magnetic Clamp System with dual Improved Heavy Small Lasers and an SRM-4. The experimental Minotaur XP pushes the armor to forty-five points with Improved Heavy Small Lasers and an SRM-5.

The Wars of Reaving produced the Minotaur Z variant, equipped with a Magnetic Clamp System and an Improved Medium Heavy Laser for Society asymmetric operations. The destruction and restructuring of multiple Clans during the Reaving disrupted production at several facilities, but the Minotaur manufacturing base was broad enough to survive the upheaval. The design remains the standard heavy ProtoMek across the surviving Homeworld Clans, its combination of firepower and protection still unmatched in the first-generation weight range.

The Orc is a four-ton second-generation ProtoMek designed by Clan Hell's Horses as their first homegrown ProtoMek design. Unveiled in 3066 after the Horses confirmed the value of first-generation ProtoMeks assimilated from the fallen Smoke Jaguars, the Orc was built with the Horses' unique combined-arms battle philosophy firmly in mind. Mounting four single-tube SRM launchers spread across the arms and torso, the Orc was specifically designed for anti-vehicle and anti-infantry work, the tactical roles the Hell's Horses have championed for centuries. The design quickly became a fixture in the Clan's frontline formations as a special attachment to every Cluster.

The Orc is built for speed and close-range saturation fire. A thirty-six-rated fusion engine drives the four-ton frame to a cruising speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, allowing it to keep pace with most Clan medium Meks. The quartet of single-tube SRM launchers, distributed between both arms and the torso, provides excellent missile coverage against multiple target types. Each arm launcher carries five rounds while the torso pair shares a ten-round magazine, giving the Orc twenty total missile salvos before exhausting its ammunition supply.

Twenty points of armor provide solid protection for a four-ton design, roughly equivalent to the five-ton Centaur and sufficient to survive several light weapon hits before structural compromise. The SRM-heavy loadout makes the Orc particularly effective against vehicles and infantry, where the cluster munitions can exploit weak armor coverage and suppression effects. Against heavier targets, a Point of Orcs can concentrate fire to achieve meaningful damage, though individual machines lack the punch to threaten heavy armor alone. The design lacks jump jets, limiting its tactical flexibility in broken terrain but keeping manufacturing costs and maintenance requirements low, consistent with the Horses' doctrine of fielding large numbers of combined-arms assets.

The Orc emerged from the Hell's Horses' post-Refusal War revitalization program under Khan James Cobb. After the Clan's initial failure to secure an Inner Sphere foothold, Cobb launched a comprehensive program to recover damaged morale and prepare the touman for an eventual return to the Occupation Zones. ProtoMek technology, initially adopted on a probationary basis following the Jaguar Annihilation, was gradually integrated into the Horses' combined-arms doctrine during this period. By 3066, the Clan's scientists had accumulated enough experience with first-generation designs to unveil a ProtoMek built from the ground up to complement the Horses' signature infantry and vehicle formations.

The Orc found immediate acceptance within the Horse touman. Every ProtoMek Star assigned to the Clan's Alpha and Beta Galaxies fielded as many as two Orcs alongside older first-generation designs. Entire Stars and even Binaries of ProtoMeks were deployed as special attachments to every frontline Cluster, with the Orc serving as the backbone of these formations. The design's emphasis on anti-vehicle and anti-infantry firepower made it a natural complement to the Horses' Elemental forces, and the two unit types quickly developed cooperative tactics that leveraged their respective strengths.

The Horses' success with the Orc drew unwanted attention. Recent observations have shown a sharp decline in ProtoMek deployment across the Horses' entire touman following a rash of raids by unidentified Clan forces in and around their Occupation Zone. The mysterious invaders, fielding ProtoMeks of their own, focused their attacks on lesser objectives the Horses commonly assigned only a few Points to garrison. It is largely presumed that many of the Horses' own ProtoMeks fell victim to these attackers, who appeared to be Homeworld Clans eager to capitalize on the Horses' success and the chaos of the Jihad for their own ends.

Despite these losses, the Hell's Horses continued developing Orc variants throughout the late 3060s and into the Jihad era. The Orc 2 entered production in 3067 as a long-range fire support variant, while the Orc 3 and Orc 4 represented different approaches to maximizing close-range firepower. The design remains central to the Horses' ProtoMek doctrine, and replacement production at the Industriplex Upsilon on Niles has maintained steady output to offset combat losses.

The Procyon is a five-ton second-generation ProtoMek designed by Clan Coyote, among the first Clans to stage Trials on Huntress for ProtoMek technology after the Smoke Jaguar Annihilation. Originally conceived as a quadruped design in the Coyotes' effort to reclaim their former reputation as the innovator Clan, practical limitations with both the technology and pilot adaptation forced Coyote engineers to re-envision their debut machine with a conventional humanoid configuration. The Procyon entered full-scale production after three years of testing, emerging as a versatile energy-weapon platform built to support heavier BattleMek and Elemental formations with maximum field endurance.

The base Procyon combines good mobility with an energy weapon payload designed for maximum operational endurance. A forty-five-rated fusion engine drives the five-ton frame at sixty-four kilometers per hour cruising speed, and twin ER Small Lasers mounted in the arms provide reliable firepower without ammunition dependency. Four heat sinks manage the thermal load from sustained laser fire, allowing a Procyon Point to maintain continuous engagement without overheating concerns. Twenty points of armor provide adequate protection, comparable to many first-generation designs of similar mass.

The Procyon's all-energy weapons configuration gives it virtually unlimited combat endurance, a significant advantage during extended operations where resupply is uncertain. A Point of five Procyons puts ten ER Small Lasers on target, sufficient to threaten light Meks and overwhelm battle armor formations. The design lacks jump jets in its base configuration, limiting terrain flexibility, but several variants address this deficiency. Commanders typically deploy Procyon Points alongside heavier Mek formations, where the ProtoMeks provide flanking fire and clean up damaged targets while the main force absorbs enemy attention.

The Procyon's development history reflects the Coyotes' ambition to push ProtoMek technology beyond the boundaries established by the Smoke Jaguars. After winning Trials of Possession for ProtoMek production data on Huntress, Coyote scientists immediately launched several development projects. Their first concept was an innovative quadruped chassis that would have given the design superior stability and ground speed, but pilot adaptation issues and manufacturing limitations forced a retreat to conventional humanoid configuration. The resulting Procyon, while less revolutionary than intended, proved to be a solid and reliable design that validated the Coyotes' ProtoMek ambitions.

ProtoMek Stars in the Coyotes' Alpha and Epsilon Galaxies fielded brand-new Procyons in Point-sized formations within a year of the design's introduction. The Procyon also appeared in the Hell's Horses touman by 3066, suggesting collaboration between the two Clans at some stage of development. The Coyotes' shared their ProtoMek expertise in exchange for the Horses' extensive experience with combined-arms integration, a partnership that benefited both Clans' ProtoMek programs.

The Coyotes subsequently experienced a surge in ProtoMek development that produced multiple Procyon variants in rapid succession. The Procyon 2 traded the energy weapons for twin LRM-4 launchers and additional armor, creating a dedicated fire support variant. The Procyon 3 mounted a Heavy Small Laser alongside an LRM-3, combining close-range punch with indirect fire capability. The Procyon 4 used a Streak SRM-3 and machine gun combination for efficient close combat, while the Procyon 5 incorporated five jump jets alongside an ER Small Laser and SRM-2 for maximum tactical flexibility.

The quadruped concept was eventually realized by Clan Hell's Horses, who applied Coyote innovation to produce the Procyon Quad variant on Csesztreg. This six-ton design fulfilled the original vision of a four-legged ProtoMek, mounting AP Gauss Rifles and an SRM-2 launcher on a chassis that offered twenty percent more speed and fifty percent more armor than the bipedal original. The Wars of Reaving produced one final variant when the Society developed the Procyon Z, a jump-capable design equipped with a Magnetic Clamp System for OmniMek transport. Following the destruction of the Society, the surviving Procyon production lines continued operating under their respective Clan owners, and the design remains in active service across the Homeworld Clans.

The Roc is a seven-ton first-generation ProtoMek developed by Clan Smoke Jaguar as the backbone of the original ProtoMek program on Huntress. Widely regarded as the most successful design to emerge from the program, the Roc combines mobility, armor, and firepower more effectively than any of its siblings, making it suitable for a wide variety of attack and defense missions. Built around an ER Medium Laser and five jump jets, the Roc delivers BattleMek-grade firepower from a platform capable of traversing nearly any terrain. Its balance of capabilities made it the most commonly fielded ProtoMek in the Homeworld Clans by the mid-3060s, forming the core of most mixed ProtoMek formations.

The Roc primary weapon is its ER Medium Laser, a weapon that would be respectable on a light BattleMek and is devastating on a seven-ton ProtoMek. The extended-range variant allows engagement at distances where most ProtoMek opponents cannot effectively return fire, giving the Roc a significant tactical advantage in open terrain. Five jump jets provide one hundred and fifty meters of jumping distance, allowing the Roc to exploit terrain features, clear obstacles, and execute flanking maneuvers that ground-bound opponents cannot counter. The sixty-rated fusion engine delivers fifty-four kilometers per hour cruising speed, adequate for keeping pace with medium-weight formations.

The Roc armor protection of thirty-one points is among the best for first-generation ProtoMeks of its weight class, sufficient to absorb multiple medium weapon hits before structural compromise. As an energy-only design, the base Roc has no ammunition dependency, allowing indefinite combat endurance limited only by pilot fatigue and heat buildup. The Roc only significant limitation is the single-weapon loadout, which means a weapon hit or targeting system malfunction reduces the design to a very expensive paperweight. Despite this vulnerability, the Roc ratio of mobility to firepower and its all-around competence have made it the measuring stick against which other ProtoMek designs are judged.

The Roc was conceived by Smoke Jaguar scientists as the primary combat ProtoMek in the original lineup, designed to balance all the competing demands of speed, protection, and firepower in a single chassis. Where other designs in the program specialized in reconnaissance, anti-infantry work, or heavy fire support, the Roc was intended to be the generalist, capable of performing adequately in any role. The decision to build it around an ER Medium Laser rather than a missile or ballistic weapon reflected the Jaguar scientists emphasis on reliability and endurance over burst damage potential.

The Roc combat debut during the Battle of Huntress in 3060 validated the design philosophy. In the varied terrain of Huntress, from dense jungle to rocky highlands, the Roc jump jets allowed it to operate effectively everywhere while its ER Medium Laser engaged targets at ranges that kept the fragile ProtoMek frame outside the effective envelope of most small arms. Multiple Points of Rocs were credited with delaying Inner Sphere advances long enough for Jaguar forces to establish secondary defensive positions, their combination of firepower and mobility making them difficult targets to pin down.

Following the Jaguar Annihilation, the Roc became arguably the most sought-after ProtoMek design. Virtually every Clan that acquired ProtoMek technology prioritized Roc production, recognizing it as the most versatile and capable design available. Clan Snow Raven established a major production line at the Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on Dante, while Clan Wolf began manufacturing Rocs at Csesztreg. Clan Goliath Scorpion continued production at the original Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress, and several other Clans established smaller production runs at various facilities.

The Roc has inspired more variant configurations than any other first-generation ProtoMek. The Roc 2 mounts a Heavy Medium Laser for increased close-range damage. The Roc 3 trades jump jets for a Medium Pulse Laser and heavier armor. The Roc 4 combines an ECM Suite with an AP Gauss Rifle for electronic warfare capability. The Roc 5 pushes jump capability to seven jets with a Medium Chemical Laser. Each variant reflects a different Clan tactical philosophy applied to the proven Roc chassis.

The Wars of Reaving saw the Society produce the Roc Z variant at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex, equipped with a Magnetic Clamp System for OmniMek transport and a Medium Chemical Laser. The upheaval of the Reaving disrupted several Roc production lines as Clans were absorbed or destroyed, but the design broad production base ensured continuity. The Roc remains the single most commonly fielded ProtoMek design across the surviving Homeworld Clans, its versatility and proven combat record ensuring that it will remain in production for decades to come.

shared: The Satyr is a four-ton first-generation ProtoMek developed as the last design completed in the original Clan Smoke Jaguar ProtoMek program on Huntress. Designed for deep-penetration reconnaissance, the Satyr combines high ground speed with an ER Small Laser and a light active probe, giving it the ability to detect hidden units while operating far from friendly support. The inclusion of electronic detection equipment makes the Satyr unique among first-generation ProtoMeks, as most contemporary designs mounted only weapons and armor. By the mid-3060s, the Satyr had become one of the most widely produced reconnaissance ProtoMeks in the Homeworld Clans, valued for its ability to locate enemies that heavier units could then engage.

The Satyr primary asset is its light active probe, which extends detection range and can reveal hidden units that would otherwise achieve surprise against friendly forces. The ER Small Laser provides reliable firepower without ammunition dependency, allowing the Satyr to operate for extended periods without resupply. A forty-five-rated fusion engine drives the four-ton frame at seventy-six kilometers per hour cruising speed with a flank speed approaching one hundred and thirteen, making the Satyr fast enough to outrun most heavy and assault class BattleMeks while remaining slower than dedicated speedsters like the Siren.

Armor protection is the Satyr most significant weakness, with only twelve points distributed across the frame. This is barely sufficient to survive a single medium laser hit, and concentrated fire from even conventional infantry can threaten the design. The Satyr mounts no jump jets in its base configuration, limiting terrain navigation options. Commanders typically deploy Satyr Points as the eyes of larger formations, pushing them forward to identify enemy positions while keeping heavier ProtoMeks and BattleMeks in reserve to exploit the intelligence gathered. The Satyr is emphatically not a combat design, and pilots who forget this distinction tend to have short careers.

The Satyr was the final design completed in the original Smoke Jaguar ProtoMek program before the Battle of Huntress in 3060. Jaguar scientists developed it to address a critical capability gap: the existing ProtoMek lineup lacked organic electronic warfare and detection capability. While the Siren provided raw speed for visual reconnaissance, the Satyr offered something more sophisticated, the ability to detect concealed enemies and feed targeting data to heavier units. The light active probe was a significant engineering challenge to miniaturize for the ProtoMek chassis, and the Satyr development ran right up to the eve of Task Force Serpent invasion.

During the Battle of Huntress, the Satyr saw limited deployment due to the small number of units completed before the invasion. Those that did see action proved their worth in the defensive fighting around the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex, where their probes detected Inner Sphere special forces teams attempting to infiltrate Jaguar defensive positions. Khan Osis reportedly expressed particular satisfaction with the Satyr after witnessing its sensor capability in action, though this could not prevent the Clan ultimate defeat.

Post-Annihilation, the Satyr became one of the most sought-after ProtoMek designs precisely because of its detection capability. Clan Coyote invested heavily in Satyr production, recognizing that ProtoMek formations without organic reconnaissance assets were operating blind. Clan Jade Falcon also acquired Satyr production data and integrated the design into their garrison forces along the Periphery border, where detecting Dark Caste raiders was a constant requirement. Clan Hell Horses established production at Industriplex Upsilon on Niles, valuing the Satyr for its combined-arms reconnaissance doctrine.

Variant development has focused on enhancing the Satyr combat capability while retaining its reconnaissance role. The Satyr 2 adds seven jump jets and replaces the ER Small Laser with a Micro Pulse Laser, creating a highly mobile variant that can reach terrain inaccessible to ground-bound units. The Satyr 3 mounts a Streak SRM-2 with five jump jets, adding meaningful anti-armor punch. The Satyr 4 replaces the probe with a Light TAG designator and AP Gauss Rifle, converting the design into a target spotter for artillery and guided munitions.

The experimental Satyr XP, produced under Clan Jade Falcon supervision, pushes the chassis to its limits with nine jump jets providing an extraordinary two hundred and seventy meters of jumping range. Armed only with an SRM-2, the XP variant trades nearly all combat capability for unmatched terrain mobility. The Wars of Reaving disrupted several Satyr production lines, but the design remains in active manufacture across the surviving Homeworld Clans, its reconnaissance capability ensuring continued relevance even as newer designs enter service.

The Siren is a three-ton first-generation ProtoMek designed by Clan Smoke Jaguar as the fastest ground unit in the original ProtoMek program. Built around an oversized forty-five-rated fusion engine that accounts for a third of the machine total mass, the Siren achieves a cruising speed of one hundred and eight kilometers per hour, outpacing virtually every ground-based combat unit short of a hovercraft. This extraordinary speed comes at the cost of nearly everything else: the Siren carries only minimal armor and a pair of light machine guns, making it almost useless in direct combat against anything heavier than conventional infantry. Its intended role as a forward scout and spotter for heavier ProtoMek formations leverages its one overwhelming advantage to compensate for its many limitations.

Speed defines the Siren. Its forty-five-rated engine pushes the three-ton frame to a flank speed approaching one hundred and sixty-two kilometers per hour, making it the fastest ProtoMek ever produced and one of the fastest ground combat units in any arsenal. A pair of light machine guns provide suppressive capability against unarmored targets, though they pose no meaningful threat to battle armor or armored vehicles. The Siren carries twelve points of armor, barely sufficient to survive a single medium laser hit, and mounts no jump jets.

The Siren excels in exactly one role: high-speed reconnaissance. A Point of Sirens can cover enormous distances in minimal time, identifying enemy positions and calling in strikes from heavier assets before the opposition can react. The design is catastrophically vulnerable to interception, however, as any hit that penetrates its thin armor is likely to cause critical damage. Pilots learn quickly that the Siren survival depends entirely on maintaining speed and avoiding engagement. Those who stop moving or attempt to stand and fight rarely survive the experience. In combined-arms formations, Sirens typically operate well ahead of the main body, providing real-time intelligence that allows heavier ProtoMeks and BattleMeks to maneuver into advantageous positions.

The Siren emerged from the Smoke Jaguar ProtoMek program as the dedicated reconnaissance design, filling a critical gap in the original lineup between the light Harpy and the combat-oriented Satyr. Jaguar scientists recognized early that ProtoMek formations would need organic scouting capability, and the Siren was designed from the ground up to maximize speed at the expense of all other considerations. The oversized engine that gives the Siren its remarkable performance was considered an engineering extravagance by some, but the resulting speed proved invaluable during testing.

During the Battle of Huntress in 3060, Sirens were among the first ProtoMeks deployed against Task Force Serpent. Their extreme speed allowed them to serve as couriers and scouts in the chaotic jungle fighting, carrying messages between Jaguar positions when communications were disrupted by Inner Sphere electronic warfare. Several Siren Points also conducted harassment raids against Serpent supply lines, using their speed to strike and withdraw before the surprised Inner Sphere troops could organize a response.

After the Jaguar Annihilation, the Siren was acquired by multiple Clans alongside other ProtoMek designs. Clan Snow Raven showed particular interest in the Siren, valuing its reconnaissance capability for the naval-oriented Clan long-range patrol doctrine. Clan Coyote also produced significant numbers of Sirens, finding the design useful for rapid response garrison duty on their scattered Homeworld enclaves. The simplicity of the Siren chassis and its reliance on readily available light machine guns made it one of the easier ProtoMek designs to manufacture.

Variant development for the Siren has focused on alternative weapon fits and incremental speed adjustments. The Siren 2 replaces the light machine guns with standard machine guns for marginally better anti-infantry punch. The Siren 3 trades engine capacity for a pair of SRM-1 launchers, giving it limited anti-armor capability at the cost of reduced speed. The Siren 4 incorporates a myomer booster and ER Micro Laser, maintaining the high-speed profile while adding an ammunition-independent weapon. The Siren 5 mounts an AP Gauss Rifle, the most recent variant designed for anti-battle-armor operations.

The Siren remains in production across the Homeworld Clans, though its role has been partially supplanted by faster second-generation designs like the Cecerops. Still, the Siren low manufacturing cost and proven reliability ensure continued demand, particularly among Clans that maintain large garrison forces across multiple worlds. The design is most commonly encountered in mixed reconnaissance Points paired with heavier ProtoMeks that provide the combat power the Siren itself lacks.

The Svartalfa is a fourteen-ton ultraheavy ProtoMek developed by Clan Hell's Horses, representing a radical leap in ProtoMek design philosophy. Initially mistaken for a light or ultralight LAM by intelligence analysts due to its flight capability, the Svartalfa is in fact an enormous ProtoMek equipped with a wing-in-ground effect gliding system that allows limited low-altitude flight at speeds exceeding sixty kilometers per hour. At half again the mass of any previously known ProtoMek, the Svartalfa mounts more armor than most twenty-ton BattleMeks and carries a weapons suite that can challenge medium Meks in direct combat. The design's existence was first revealed when Clan Wolf became an unwitting live-fire test subject, and the Wolves struggled to understand what they were facing: too small to be a Mek, but far too tough to be battle armor or any known ProtoMek.

The Svartalfa's most distinctive feature is its wing-in-ground effect gliding system. While incapable of true flight or transformation like a Land-Air Mek, the Svartalfa uses deployable wings to glide just above the ground surface at cruising speeds of forty-three kilometers per hour, with a flank speed approaching sixty-five. On foot, the massive ProtoMek moves at a crawl barely exceeding ten kilometers per hour, making the gliding mode essential for tactical maneuvering. The wings fold compactly for ground operations and transport, and their robust construction allows them to absorb weapons fire without significantly degrading gliding performance.

The Svartalfa's weapons suite punches well above its weight class. Twin arm-mounted Medium Chemical Lasers deliver damage comparable to Inner Sphere medium lasers without requiring the heat dissipation systems that standard energy weapons demand, though their chemical fuel supply limits operational endurance to approximately thirty salvos total. A Streak SRM-6 launcher in the main gun mount provides devastating close-range firepower with ten guided salvos, while a torso-mounted machine gun with fifty rounds handles anti-infantry work. Sixty-four points of armor can survive a heavy Gauss rifle hit to the torso at point-blank range, making the Svartalfa extraordinarily resilient for any combat unit below twenty tons. The cockpit is fifty percent larger than standard ProtoMek designs, allowing pilots of Elemental phenotype to operate the machine, though it can be reconfigured for smaller pilots as well.

Intelligence gathered from Diamond Shark trade delegations first hinted at the Svartalfa's existence through rumors of Clan Hell's Horses developing a light or ultralight LAM. One distant image was obtained showing a flying object, but covert missions to ferret out more information all ended in failure. The truth was revealed when the Horses deployed the Svartalfa against Clan Wolf in live combat, leaving the Wolves thoroughly confused about what they faced. Too small for a Mek but far too durable for any known battle armor or ProtoMek, the Svartalfa took considerable time and casualties before Wolf warriors learned to counter it effectively.

The Svartalfa has been distributed exclusively to the Hell's Horses' best ProtoMek pilots in elite units. In raids against the Wolves, the design proved its worth both in direct combat and in the confusion it sowed. Deploying medium and heavy Meks to engage even a single ProtoMek frustrated Wolf MekWarriors, while attempts to counter with battle armor failed due to the Svartalfa's decisive advantages in armor, firepower, and mobility. The design provides a low-resource unit that can tie down far more complex opponents, freeing heavier forces to concentrate on fewer targets.

A dedicated fire support variant, the Svartalfa 2, was developed by Hell's Horses scientists who managed to mount dual fifteen-tube long-range missile racks, one in the torso and one as a main gun. This required significant armor reduction but provided devastating long-range barrage capability. A Point of LRM-equipped Svartalfas with a forward spotter once convinced a Star of Wolf Meks that they were engaging a Bane hiding in the woods, rotating the spotter position to keep the Wolves guessing while ravaging them with indirect fire. The Svartalfa 3 takes a different approach, mounting five Medium Chemical Lasers for sustained energy-weapon engagements at the cost of the Streak launcher and machine gun.

The Triton is an eight-ton second-generation ProtoMek designed by Clan Goliath Scorpion to complement their Seeker tradition. After a string of humbling failures following the Great Refusal, the Scorpions leveraged resources acquired through overtures to the Snow Ravens to jump-start their faltering ProtoMek program. The resulting Triton was purpose-built to efficiently accompany the solitary warriors dedicated to carrying on the Seeker mandate, combining robust armor protection, full jump capability, and ammunition-efficient weaponry in a heavy ProtoMek frame optimized for independent extended operations.

The Triton's primary armament is a Streak SRM-4 launcher mounted in the main gun position, fed by ten volleys of ammunition. The Streak system ensures every missile hits its target, making the Triton one of the most ammunition-efficient missile platforms among ProtoMek designs. The system's lock-on-or-don't-fire logic means that each trigger pull either delivers a full four-missile salvo or conserves the ammunition entirely, a significant advantage during the extended independent operations the Seeker tradition demands. A torso-mounted ER Micro Laser provides backup firepower for the unlikely event the Streak magazines run dry.

Four jump jets provide one hundred twenty meters of leaping distance, giving the eight-ton design terrain mobility unusual for its weight class. Almost two tons of armor at thirty-eight points provide excellent protection, allowing the Triton to survive hits from heavy weapons that would destroy lighter ProtoMeks outright. The combination of heavy armor, efficient weapons, and jump capability makes the Triton one of the most self-sufficient ProtoMek designs in service, capable of sustained independent operations that mirror the Seeker tradition it was built to serve. Cruising speed of forty-three kilometers per hour is modest, but the jump jets compensate for the lack of ground speed in tactical situations.

The Triton emerged from the Goliath Scorpion's post-Great Refusal rebuilding effort. The Clan's overtures to the Snow Ravens netted them critical resources that allowed the creation of a new Galaxy dedicated to the Seeker tradition and the revitalization of their ProtoMek program. Named for the aquatic predator, the Triton was designed from the ground up to serve alongside Seeker warriors, emphasizing operational endurance and self-sufficiency over raw firepower or speed.

The Triton was included in the recently deployed Chi Galaxy, where it served alongside Seeker warriors without the friction that plagued other Scorpion ProtoMek deployments. In second-line units, however, the introduction of Tritons as replacements for Elemental units that had successfully tested out to frontline postings created significant resentment. ProtoMek pilots felt denigrated at being automatically placed below solahma warriors in the Clan's hierarchy, and several declared Trials of Refusal against battle armor units being promoted to frontline status.

These internal tensions did not prevent the development of multiple variants. The Triton 2 replaced the Streak launcher with an LRM-3, ER Small Laser, and additional Micro Lasers, creating a more versatile engagement profile suited to varied mission requirements. Two more specialized variants appeared just before the HPG blackout, both employing Heavy Laser technology. The Triton 3 stripped the entire weapons suite for a single Heavy Medium Laser, sacrificing versatility for devastating single-shot punch and complete ammunition independence. The Triton 4 mounted Heavy Small Lasers in each arm with an ER Micro Laser in the torso, distributing close-range heavy firepower across multiple locations.

The Eridani Light Horse captured a group of seven Triton ProtoMeks during initial Trials of Possession at Lootera, forming them into an augmented point dubbed the "Seven Deadly Sins." The group remained appreciative of the Light Horse's respectful treatment, reciprocating by zealously briefing and training the mercenaries in anti-ProtoMek tactics using both simulator and live-fire exercises. Their fate following the HPG blackout remains unknown alongside the rest of the Light Horse contingent in Clan space.

text.overview: The Basilisk is a seven-ton second-generation ProtoMek produced by Clan Cloud Cobra to provide reliable heavy fire support for armored infantry and BattleMek formations. With firepower to match some light BattleMeks and nearly two full tons of armor protection, the Basilisk serves as a significant step up in combat capability from the lighter ProtoMek designs. Unusual for a Clan war machine, the Basilisk's trademark is sturdiness and reliability rather than speed or innovation, reflecting the Cloud Cobras' pragmatic approach to integrating ProtoMek technology into their ground forces.
text.deployment: The Basilisk 2 fundamentally reimagines the design as a close-quarters brawler. The ER Medium Laser gives way to an ER Small Laser in the torso and ER Micro Lasers in each arm, while an SRM-2 launcher in the main gun mount with ten rounds replaces the LRM-3. Four body-mounted jump jets provide one hundred twenty meters of leaping distance, addressing the base model's terrain limitations. Armor drops to thirty-four points to accommodate the jump jets and expanded weapons suite. This variant is commonly assigned to the most aggressive ProtoMek pilots in Beta Galaxy, who exploit the jump capability to close rapidly with opponents and overwhelm them with the diverse close-range weapons package. First tested by warriors of Alpha Galaxy's 149th Cobra Guards, the Basilisk 2 was most fully adopted by Beta Galaxy.
text.battleHistory:
Produced at Complex H-6 CCC on Homer, the Basilisk was slow to appear in the Cloud Cobra touman but has become a steady presence once its worth was proven. The design was specifically built to answer the Cloud Cobras' need for more reliable and powerful ground forces to support their heavy Elemental and BattleMek formations. The recent fighting in and around the Tanite worlds provided extensive combat experience, establishing the Basilisk as one of the most dependable ProtoMeks in the Cloud Cobra arsenal.

The Basilisk's successes attracted attention from other Clans, most particularly the Steel Vipers, who challenged for several Points' worth of ProtoMeks. The last reports received from the Clan Homeworlds indicated that the Cloud Cobras were increasing both production and deployment of the Basilisk and their other ProtoMek designs, a response to the escalating violence that characterized the pre-Reaving period.

Beta Galaxy embraced the Basilisk most fully, adopting the design in all its forms and developing the close-combat Basilisk 2 variant for their most aggressive ProtoMek pilots. The Basilisk 2 replaced the ER Medium Laser with a combination of ER Small and ER Micro Lasers alongside SRM-2s and jump jets, creating a brawler configuration fundamentally different from the base model's long-range fire support role. A third variant, the Basilisk 3, mounted extended jump jets for enhanced terrain mobility while retaining the powerful ER Medium Laser.

Diamond Shark merchants eventually acquired at least one Basilisk, and Warrior Khaled operated as part of a mixed ProtoMek Point in the Sharks' Deep Periphery forces. Sighted on Twycross in 3073 during a Trial between the Crusader Wolves and Diamond Sharks, Khaled's Basilisk served as the anchor of his Point while lighter ProtoMeks harassed the opposition. His Point accounted for three OmniMek kills despite ultimately losing the Trial, demonstrating the Basilisk's value as a fire support platform even in unfavorable matchups.
