text.deployment: The base Cecerops mounts a single ER Micro Laser in the torso, providing ammunition-independent firepower that allows extended operations without resupply. The forty-five-rated engine dominates the three-ton chassis, producing a cruising speed of ninety-seven kilometers per hour that makes the Cecerops one of the fastest ground combat units in any Clan arsenal. Fourteen points of armor provide adequate protection for the weight class. Without jump jets, the design relies entirely on its extraordinary ground speed to navigate terrain and evade threats. Produced at the Blood Spirit Reserve Industriplex-2 on York, the Cecerops is found predominantly among Blood Spirit forces, with limited numbers shipped to the Snow Ravens before 3071.

The most widely used Blood Spirit variant, the Cecerops 2 trades a fraction of engine power for a torso-mounted Streak SRM-1 launcher with ten rounds of ammunition-efficient guided missiles. The reduced engine drops cruising speed to eighty-six kilometers per hour, still remarkably fast but a noticeable step down from the base model. Armor protection remains at fourteen points. The Streak system ensures no missile is wasted, making the Cecerops 2 more resource-efficient in sustained engagements than conventional missile-armed ProtoMeks. This variant was developed during the constant clashes with the Star Adders on Arcadia and Albion, where ammunition conservation became a critical concern for the embattled Blood Spirits.

The Cecerops 3 further reduces engine size to mount a heavier SRM-2 launcher in the torso with eleven rounds of ammunition. Cruising speed drops to seventy-five kilometers per hour, and the cockpit is completely restructured to accommodate the larger missile system, making the variant exceedingly cramped even by ProtoMek standards. Armor dips slightly to thirteen points. This configuration is not favored by most Cecerops pilots due to the uncomfortable cockpit modifications, though warriors of the McFadden bloodline tend to gravitate toward the Cecerops 3, their smaller body type proving more comfortable in the compacted space. The increased missile punch makes this variant more viable against armored targets at the cost of the signature speed that defines the Cecerops line.

The Cecerops 4 was reportedly detected among the mysterious gray-painted attackers that struck multiple Clan economic centers in the Falcon and Horse Occupation Zones in late 3073. Mounting a Micro Pulse Laser in the torso and matching the speed of the Streak-armed Cecerops 2 at eighty-six kilometers per hour cruising, this variant trades range for improved accuracy at close quarters. Armor drops to eleven points, the lightest of any Cecerops configuration, and the head takes on a decidedly skeletal visage that reinforces the raptor-like aesthetic. The identity of the forces fielding this variant and its manufacturing origin remain among the enduring mysteries of the Jihad-era Homeworld conflicts.

The Cecerops 5 is a radical departure from the speed-focused design philosophy of the original. Equipped with a Magnetic Clamp System for OmniMek transport and an AP Gauss Rifle with twelve rounds of ammunition, this variant sacrifices the Cecerops' legendary speed entirely, cruising at just forty-three kilometers per hour. Armor returns to fourteen points, matching the base model. The Magnetic Clamp allows the Cecerops 5 to ride into battle attached to an OmniMek, deploying at close range to use the AP Gauss Rifle against infantry and battle armor formations. This configuration reflects a fundamentally different tactical doctrine, transforming the Cecerops from an independent high-speed interceptor into a transported fire support asset.

text.overview: The Centaur is a five-ton first-generation ProtoMech developed by Clan Smoke Jaguar scientists at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress as part of the original ProtoMech program initiated in the late 3050s. Designed as a versatile light fire support platform capable of engaging targets across multiple range bands, the Centaur proved itself one of the most adaptable designs to emerge from the Jaguar program. Its combination of missile and energy armament in a compact, fast-moving frame set it apart from more specialized contemporaries such as the Harpy or Minotaur. By the mid-3060s, the Centaur was in active production for at least five different Clans, proof of the soundness of its underlying design and its value as a flexible screening element in Clan combined-arms formations.
text.deployment: Introduced in 3063, this variant replaces the LRM-3 with a Heavy Small Laser while retaining the SRM-2 launcher, trading long-range capability for a devastating close-range energy weapon that requires no ammunition. The Heavy Small Laser generates significant heat for a ProtoMech-scale weapon but delivers damage equivalent to a standard medium laser at short range, making a Point of this variant extremely dangerous in close quarters. Armor protection is marginally improved over the base model with twenty-one points of coverage. Production was established at the Csesztreg Industriplex Epsilon under Clan Wolf and at Kindraa Payne-Beyl-Grant’s facility on Shadow, the latter representing one of the few ProtoMech production lines operated by Clan Fire Mandrill before their destruction during the Wars of Reaving.

text.deployment: First manufactured in 3065, this radical redesign strips all missile systems and the micro laser in favor of a single ER Medium Laser mounted in the torso. The removal of all ammunition-dependent weapons eliminates the endurance problems that plague the base Centaur, giving this variant theoretically unlimited combat persistence. However, this comes at a severe cost: armor protection drops to just fifteen points, leaving the frame critically vulnerable to concentrated fire. A single PPC hit to the center torso will cripple the unit. The ER Medium Laser’s effective range and consistent damage output make this variant best suited to hit-and-run strikes where its speed can compensate for its fragility. Produced exclusively at the Aeroyard Gargain on Bearclaw, initially under Clan Snow Raven and later transferred to Clan Stone Lion following the Raven’s relocation to the Inner Sphere.

The base Chrysaor distributes four ER Micro Lasers across the frame, with one in each arm and two in the torso. This weapons distribution ensures combat capability is maintained even after localized damage. Four heat sinks manage the thermal load from sustained laser fire. Twenty-eight points of armor provide the strongest protection of any six-ton ProtoMek, sufficient to absorb multiple light weapon hits. The fifty-five-rated engine drives the frame at sixty-four kilometers per hour cruising speed without jump jets. Produced at both the Blood Spirit Reserve Industriplex-2 on York and the Snow Raven Aeroyard Gargain on Bearclaw, the base Chrysaor serves in both Clans' ProtoMek formations and has spread to limited numbers of Diamond Shark and pirate forces.
text.battleHistory:
The Chrysaor was conceived alongside the Cecerops as part of the Blood Spirit and Snow Raven ProtoMek development partnership. While the lighter design reached production first, the Chrysaor proved worth the additional development time as a more capable combat platform. However, its debut on Arcadia nearly ended the program before it truly began. Star Colonel Suzanne Church of the 171st Crimson Guards commanded a full Trinary of Chrysaors and Cecerops but fundamentally misunderstood how to employ ProtoMeks, treating them as oversized Elementals rather than independent combat machines. When her tactical failures were predictably attributed to the machines themselves, a Chrysaor pilot named Andre stepped forward to challenge Church to a Trial of Grievance.

The Trial proved decisive. Fought in front of other Star Colonels and the troops of the 171st, Church could not refuse without losing honor. Despite fighting augmented, Church fell to Andre's clever use of the Chrysaor's mobility and firepower, simultaneously vindicating the design and exposing the Star Colonel's tactical incompetence. Andre's promotion that followed created a champion for ProtoMek acceptance among the Blood Spirit warrior caste, and the Chrysaor gradually earned the respect its capabilities deserved.

Both Blood Spirit and Snow Raven use the Chrysaor extensively in their ProtoMek forces. The Ravens have exported some units to their Inner Sphere operations, though one shipment of a full Star was raided by unknown pirates suspected of operating from Antallos. Diamond Shark merchants also acquired Chrysaors at bargain prices following erroneous reports of the design's poor showing on Arcadia, keeping a Point as a demonstration unit while selling others to Clans in the Inner Sphere. On Circe, Snow Raven Chrysaors of the Second Raven Garrison Cluster successfully repelled a Goliath Scorpion incursion, using their superior mobility to encircle Elemental formations and tear into them with massed laser fire until a late-arriving Griffin IIC turned the battle.

A close-combat variant, the Chrysaor 2, replaced the quad ER Micro Lasers with dual Micro Pulse Lasers and added five jump jets, trading sustained firepower for enhanced accuracy and terrain mobility. The variant was developed to address the Chrysaor's vulnerability in close terrain where its speed advantage could not be fully exploited.

text.deployment: The Chrysaor 2 replaces the four ER Micro Lasers with two Micro Pulse Lasers, one in the right arm and one in the torso. The reduction in weapons and heat management systems frees mass for five body-mounted jump jets providing one hundred fifty meters of leaping distance. Armor remains at twenty-eight points, unchanged from the base model. The Micro Pulse Lasers offer improved accuracy at short range compared to the ER Micro Lasers, and the jump capability transforms the Chrysaor 2 into a close-combat specialist capable of exploiting terrain features denied to the base variant. This configuration addresses the original Chrysaor's weakness in restrictive terrain, where ground speed alone cannot provide adequate tactical positioning.

text.deployment: The base Delphyne mounts a Medium Pulse Laser in the torso, providing accurate and reliable damage output without ammunition dependency. Five body-mounted jump jets give one hundred fifty meters of leaping distance, and the seventy-five-rated engine drives the nine-ton frame at fifty-four kilometers per hour cruising speed. Forty-two points of armor provide the best protection of any standard Delphyne variant. Four heat sinks manage the pulse laser's thermal output effectively. The design is found mainly in the toumans of the Blood Spirits and Fire Mandrills, produced at both the Fire Mandrill Kraftwerk on Shadow under Kindraa Payne-Beyl-Grant and the Blood Spirit facility on York.

The Delphyne 2 diversifies the weapons load significantly, replacing the Medium Pulse Laser with dual SRM-3 launchers in the torso and ER Micro Lasers in each arm. Twenty rounds of SRM ammunition provide ten salvos per launcher, giving the variant substantial short-range missile capability. This comes at the cost of two points of armor, dropping protection to forty points, and introduces ammunition dependency that the base model avoids. The combination of missiles and lasers gives the Delphyne 2 a broader engagement profile than the base model, capable of delivering both kinetic and energy damage at close range. Five jump jets and cruising speed remain unchanged from the base variant.

The Delphyne 3 is not a purpose-built variant but rather a Coyote modification of captured base-model Delphynes. Coyote technicians replace the Medium Pulse Laser with an ER Medium Laser in the torso and add a right-arm Micro Pulse Laser. The ER Medium Laser provides longer effective range than the original pulse weapon, while the Micro Pulse Laser supplements close-range damage output. Armor matches the base model at forty-two points, and the jump jet configuration remains unchanged. These modified Delphynes frequently serve as command machines for Coyote Procyon Points, their superior firepower anchoring formations of lighter five-ton ProtoMeks that would otherwise lack heavy hitting capability.

The base Erinyes mounts a single SRM-1 launcher in the torso fed by five rounds of ammunition, backed by four body-mounted jump jets providing one hundred twenty meters of leaping distance. This armament is adequate only for guard duty and anti-infantry suppression, as the single missile tube cannot generate enough damage to meaningfully threaten armored targets. Ten points of armor provide marginal protection. The Erinyes' primary strength lies in its jump capability, allowing Points to exploit broken terrain for ambush tactics. First produced at CJF Factory Zone 5 on Erewhon, the design was initially distributed to Periphery border garrisons after the program's official cancellation in 3064.

Circulated through remaining Erinyes units after the program was officially shelved in 3064, the Erinyes 2 replaces the SRM launcher and jump jets with a slightly larger engine that increases ground speed to fifty-four kilometers per hour cruising. An ER Micro Laser replaces the missile system, eliminating ammunition dependency but providing even less damage output against armored targets. Armor protection drops to eight points, making the variant dangerously fragile. Pilots were given the option of retaining the original configuration or transitioning to this variant, and opinions were divided on whether the speed increase justified the loss of jump capability and what little missile punch the base model offered.

Detected during the mysterious attacks that struck multiple Falcon worlds from within between 3072 and 3074, the Erinyes 3 shares the larger engine of the Erinyes 2 but mounts a light machine gun in the torso and increases armor to twelve points, the heaviest of any Erinyes variant. Falcon Watch reports intercepted by Loki identified this configuration among the unknown forces that burned several Clan economic centers in both the Falcon and Horse Occupation Zones. The additional armor and leg protection kept the Erinyes 3 functional during the destructive city fighting on Sudeten, Blackjack, and Somerset. The identity of the forces fielding this variant and the location of its manufacture remain unknown.

text.deployment: The base Gorgon mounts a ten-tube LRM launcher in the main gun position alongside an ER Micro Laser for close defense. The LRM-10 carries twelve salvos of ammunition, providing roughly two and a half minutes of sustained bombardment at maximum rate of fire. The fifty-rated fusion engine delivers forty-three kilometers per hour cruising speed with no jump capability. Thirty-four points of armor provide solid protection. First produced at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress, the base Gorgon subsequently entered production at the Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on Dante under Clan Snow Raven and at several other Homeworld facilities.

production.manufacturer: Complex 18|Kindraa Payne-Beyl-Grant Main Production Facility|W-4 Facilities

text.deployment: The Gorgon 2 fundamentally reimagines the chassis by replacing the LRM-10 with a Medium Pulse Laser and adding four jump jets providing one hundred and twenty meters of jumping distance. This converts the Gorgon from a long-range fire support platform into a mobile direct combat unit with ammunition-independent firepower. Thirty-six points of armor slightly exceed the base model. The pulse laser improved accuracy combined with jump jet mobility makes the Gorgon 2 effective in close terrain where the base model LRM cannot be used. This variant represents the most radical departure from the original design intent.

The Gorgon 3 mounts dual SRM-4 launchers in the torso with an upgraded engine increasing cruising speed to fifty-four kilometers per hour. The twin launchers deliver eight missiles per salvo at short range, providing devastating close-range firepower that can strip armor from light BattleMeks in a single exchange. Thirty-eight points of armor offer improved protection over the base model. The Gorgon 3 lacks jump jets, relying on its improved speed to close with targets. This variant is deployed as a short-range assault unit, typically advancing behind scouts that identify targets for the Gorgon 3 to engage at optimal missile range.

The Gorgon 4 combines an AP Gauss Rifle with an SRM-6 launcher and three jump jets providing ninety meters of jumping distance. This multi-weapon configuration gives the variant effective capability against both armored and unarmored targets at close range. Forty-one points of armor, among the highest of any Gorgon variant, allow the design to absorb significant punishment. The jump jets provide tactical flexibility that the ground-bound base model lacks. The Gorgon 4 is one of the more popular variants, its balanced loadout making it suitable for a wide range of mission profiles.

The Gorgon 5 mounts a Streak LRM-5 launcher alongside a Magnetic Clamp System that allows attachment to OmniMek exteriors for rapid transport. The Streak technology ensures missiles fire only on solid lock, conserving ammunition while guaranteeing hits. Forty-three points of armor provide the highest protection of any Gorgon variant. The Magnetic Clamp enables the Gorgon 5 to be delivered directly to the battlefield by a carrier Mek, compensating for its lack of speed and jump capability. This variant emerged during the Wars of Reaving era, reflecting the evolving ProtoMek transport doctrine.

The Gorgon 6 is a specialized electronic warfare platform mounting an Angel ECM Suite alongside an AP Gauss Rifle and Myomer Booster system. The Angel ECM provides superior electronic countermeasures that degrade enemy targeting and communications across a wide area, while the Myomer Booster allows rapid repositioning to maintain optimal ECM coverage. Cruising speed is increased to fifty-four kilometers per hour. Thirty-four points of armor match the base model. The Gorgon 6 is the most technologically advanced variant, designed to operate as an electronic warfare node within mixed ProtoMek and BattleMek formations.

The original Harpy mounts a single machine gun in the torso with one hundred rounds of ammunition, backed by three body-mounted jump jets that provide ninety meters of jumping distance. This combination makes the base Harpy a competent anti-infantry platform capable of engaging conventional foot soldiers and light vehicles from unexpected angles. The machine gun exhausts its ammunition quickly in sustained engagements, typically lasting less than two minutes of continuous fire, but the Harpy is designed for hit-and-fade tactics rather than prolonged combat. First produced at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress under Clan Smoke Jaguar, the base Harpy subsequently entered limited production at several Homeworld facilities following the Jaguar Annihilation.

The Harpy 2 replaces the machine gun with an ER Micro Laser, eliminating ammunition dependency entirely at the cost of reduced anti-infantry effectiveness. The energy weapon allows extended patrols without resupply concerns, making this variant popular for garrison duty on remote Homeworld enclaves where logistics chains are unreliable. Armor protection is reduced to eight points to accommodate the weapon swap, leaving the Harpy 2 even more fragile than its predecessor. The jump jet configuration remains unchanged at three jets providing ninety meters of leaping distance. This variant was developed by Clan Wolf and saw limited production at Csesztreg before the facility changed hands during the Wars of Reaving.

The Harpy 3 serves as a fundamental rethinking of the design philosophy, sacrificing the signature jump jets for a larger engine that increases ground speed to fifty-four kilometers per hour cruising. A light machine gun replaces the standard machine gun, and armor protection increases to twelve points, the highest of any Harpy variant. Without jump capability, the Harpy 3 loses much of the original design tactical flexibility but gains the ability to keep pace with faster ProtoMek formations. This variant found favor with Clan Snow Raven, who preferred the increased speed for reconnaissance operations across the open terrain common to many Homeworld garrison postings.

The most advanced Harpy variant, the Harpy 4 incorporates a myomer booster system that dramatically increases sprint speed while retaining the original three-jump-jet configuration. Armed with a light machine gun, the design offers marginally less sustained firepower than the base model but compensates with the ability to close distances rapidly when the booster engages. Armor protection matches the original at eleven points. The myomer booster allows the Harpy 4 to execute high-speed assault runs that would be impossible for the base variant, making it more viable in offensive operations. This variant emerged during the Jihad era as myomer booster technology became more widely available across the Homeworld Clans.

text.overview: The Hippogriff is an eight-ton ProtoMek designed by the Raven Alliance around partial wing technology, making it one of the most mobile ProtoMeks ever built. The first entirely new ProtoMek developed by the Raven Alliance, the Hippogriff was born from the Ravens' need for additional ground troops and the availability of a dedicated ProtoMek transport DropShip, the Arcadia class. Special care was invested in the design's unique flight-enhanced jump capability, with the partial wing enabling the Hippogriff to leap distances that far exceed what its mass would normally allow. The quasi-totemic design, with its feathered wing profile and avian aesthetic, has become a symbol of the Raven Alliance's ProtoMek program.
text.capabilities:
The Hippogriff joins the Gorgon in the eight-ton weight bracket but takes a fundamentally different tactical approach. Where the Gorgon features heavy weaponry, the Hippogriff relies on two compact LRM-2 launchers with atypically deep ammunition bins of twenty-four rounds each, providing an exceptional forty-eight total salvos. Its primary features are extended jump jets and a feathered partial wing that enables it to leap enormous distances in standard atmosphere, adding sixty meters to each jump for a total of one hundred fifty meters of leaping distance under standard atmospheric conditions.

Thirty points of armor provide solid protection, and the Hippogriff's doctrine of maintaining range while supplying constant covering fire means it is more likely to survive engagements than more aggressive ProtoMek designs. The trade-off is limited damage output per volley; the twin LRM-2 launchers cannot inflict enough damage to seriously threaten BattleMeks without sustained concentrated fire from an entire Point. Ground speed is modest at thirty-two kilometers per hour cruising, and the partial wing is useless in vacuum or airless environments, reducing the design to average jump performance in space or on airless moons. The Hippogriff excels as a long-range support unit that uses its exceptional mobility to maintain optimal engagement distance while providing persistent covering fire.
text.deployment: The Hippogriff mounts LRM-2 launchers in each arm, each fed by a deep twenty-four-round ammunition bin providing a total of forty-eight salvos. A partial wing mounted in the torso augments five extended jump jets for one hundred fifty meters of leaping distance in standard atmosphere. The forty-rated fusion engine provides a modest thirty-two kilometers per hour cruising speed on the ground, making the jump capability essential for tactical movement. Thirty points of armor provide solid protection for the weight class. Produced at the Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on Dante, the Hippogriff serves primarily in the Raven Alliance's Gamma and Beta Galaxies, with additional units traded to Clan Hell's Horses for garrison and solahma support duties.
text.battleHistory:
The Raven Alliance restarted its ProtoMek program in the 3080s, driven by the need for additional ground troops that could be transported by the dedicated Arcadia-class DropShip. The Hippogriff was the first entirely new design produced by this renewed program, with special emphasis on the partial wing technology that would become its defining feature. Gamma Galaxy, traditionally the heaviest ProtoMek user in the Raven touman, was quick to experiment with the Hippogriff upon its first delivery in 3110, pleased to receive a long-range support unit capable of keeping pace with dedicated infighters.

The Hippogriff's first deployment was with a detachment from the Third Raven Auxiliaries guarding Milligan's World against the ManMangler mercenary command in the apparent employ of House Kurita. A Binary of Rocs, Chrysaor 2s, and Hippogriffs intercepted a mixed company of hover APCs and light Meks on the Doone Plains. The Rocs tied up the Meks while the Hippogriffs bombarded the APCs, forcing them to unload their infantry, which was promptly pinned down by the Chrysaors. The ProtoMeks outjumped the mercenaries and forced their remnants into retreat after destroying most of their infantry and two Meks.

Clan Hell's Horses soon traded for a large number of Hippogriffs, appreciating the equine aspects of its avian design. When the Twenty-first Mechanized Assault Cluster deployed them alongside other heavy ProtoMeks to repel a Clan Wolf probing attack on Harvest in 3118, the results were disappointing. Pitched against BattleMeks without appropriate support, the Hippogriff could not inflict sufficient damage on the advancing enemy, and by the time the Horses recognized their mistake there was no time to redeploy. The Horses rejected the Hippogriff as an alternative to the superheavy Svartalfa and reassigned them to support solahma units instead.

The Raven Alliance experienced its own failure when attempting to use the Hippogriff in S-Teams for void operations. The ProtoMek proved sensationally incapable in engagements on airless moons, where the partial wing was useless and its jump capability was reduced to average while ground speed remained sluggish. The design redeemed itself during Beta Galaxy's campaign to capture Sterlington and Kirbyville in May 3144. On Sterlington, the Ninth Raven Wing Cluster deployed Elementals and Afreets against dug-in elements of the Third Periphery Guard, supported only by Hippogriffs. With their partial wings ensuring superior flight control, the ProtoMeks deployed at high altitude and swooped down like their namesake, creating panic among the defenders and causing them to flee directly into Mek elements deployed in a second wave. This extremely successful use as a shock weapon greatly elevated the Hippogriff's prestige in the Raven Alliance military.

text.deployment: The base Hydra mounts a Streak SRM-3 launcher in the torso alongside a Micro Pulse Laser in the main gun mount, providing a complementary short-range weapon suite. The Streak system carries twelve rounds of ammunition, sufficient for four full salvos before depletion. The thirty-six-rated fusion engine delivers forty-three kilometers per hour cruising speed with no jump capability. Twenty-nine points of armor give the Hydra reasonable survivability for its weight class. First produced at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress, the base Hydra entered production at additional Homeworld facilities after multiple Clans acquired Smoke Jaguar ProtoMek technology following the Clan Annihilation in 3060.

The Hydra 2 upgrades the missile armament to a Streak SRM-5 and adds three jump jets providing ninety meters of jumping distance, creating a significantly more mobile platform with greater per-salvo firepower. These improvements come at a severe armor cost, with protection reduced to only fourteen points, less than half the base model coverage. The Micro Pulse Laser is removed to free tonnage for the jump system and heavier launcher. This variant is an extreme glass cannon, capable of devastating single strikes but vulnerable to any return fire. Commanders deploy the Hydra 2 exclusively in ambush roles where its jump jets allow rapid repositioning after firing.

The Hydra 3 converts the chassis into a mobile fire support platform by replacing all original armament with an LRM-6 launcher backed by five jump jets and an upgraded engine. Cruising speed increases to fifty-four kilometers per hour, and the jump jets provide one hundred and fifty meters of leaping distance. Twenty-four points of armor offer moderate protection. The LRM-6 allows the Hydra 3 to engage targets at distances far beyond the base model effective range, though the limited ammunition supply of six salvos restricts sustained bombardment. This variant is typically paired with probe-equipped scouts that provide targeting data for indirect fire.

The Hydra 4 mounts three AP Gauss Rifles, a radical weapon fit that provides exceptional sustained anti-personnel and anti-battle-armor firepower. Each rifle carries independent ammunition, giving the variant substantial endurance in prolonged engagements against infantry and light targets. Thirty-five points of armor, the highest of any Hydra variant, provide solid protection. The design retains the base model speed and lack of jump capability. The triple AP Gauss configuration makes the Hydra 4 one of the most effective anti-infantry ProtoMeks in service, capable of shredding conventional infantry formations and threatening even heavy battle armor at close range.

text.deployment: The base Minotaur mounts two ER Medium Lasers in the torso alongside three body-mounted jump jets providing ninety meters of jumping distance. The dual laser configuration delivers devastating combined firepower with no ammunition dependency, allowing the Minotaur to fight indefinitely in its preferred defensive role. The forty-five-rated fusion engine delivers a modest thirty-two kilometers per hour cruising speed. Thirty-six points of armor provide excellent protection for the weight class. First produced at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress, the base Minotaur entered production at Csesztreg Industriplex Epsilon under Clan Wolf and Industriplex Upsilon on Niles under Clan Hell Horses, among other facilities.

The Minotaur 2 replaces the dual ER Medium Lasers with an LB-X AC/2 autocannon, fundamentally changing the design combat profile from close-range energy fighter to long-range ballistic support. The LB-X can fire both standard and cluster ammunition, the latter spreading damage across a target to find weak armor points. Twenty-four points of armor represent a significant reduction from the base model, and the jump jets are removed entirely. The design retains the base model slow cruising speed. This variant is typically deployed in rear-area fire support positions where its range advantage compensates for its reduced survivability.

The Minotaur 3 converts the chassis into a mobile fire support platform by mounting an LRM-12 launcher with five jump jets and an upgraded engine. Cruising speed increases to fifty-four kilometers per hour, and the jump jets provide one hundred and fifty meters of leaping distance, making the Minotaur 3 dramatically more mobile than the base model. Thirty-four points of armor provide reasonable protection. The LRM-12 delivers heavier per-salvo bombardment than the Gorgon LRM-10, though ammunition endurance is limited. This variant is designed to deliver concentrated fire support while using its mobility to reposition between salvos.

The Minotaur P2 prototype was developed by Clan Goliath Scorpion, incorporating a Magnetic Clamp System for OmniMek transport alongside dual Improved Heavy Small Lasers and an SRM-4 launcher. This variant maximizes close-range lethality, as the Improved Heavy Small Lasers deliver exceptional damage at point-blank range while the SRM-4 adds missile punch. Forty-five points of armor, the highest of any Minotaur variant, allow the P2 to survive in the close-range engagements its weapon suite demands. The Magnetic Clamp enables rapid delivery to the battlefield via carrier Mek, compensating for the loss of jump jets. The P2 was produced at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress.

The experimental Minotaur XP was developed under Clan Star Adder oversight as a maximum-protection close-combat variant. Mounting dual Improved Heavy Small Lasers alongside an SRM-5 launcher, the XP delivers devastating short-range firepower from behind forty-five points of armor. The SRM-5 provides the heaviest single missile salvo available on a ProtoMek chassis. Jump jets and the Magnetic Clamp System are both absent, leaving the XP dependent on its slow ground speed to reach engagement range. This experimental variant demonstrated the potential of improved weapon technology on the heavy ProtoMek platform.

The base Orc distributes four single-tube SRM launchers across the frame, with one launcher in each arm and two in the torso. Each arm launcher carries five rounds while the torso pair shares a ten-round magazine, providing twenty total salvos before ammunition exhaustion. This distribution ensures that damage to any single location does not eliminate the Orc's entire weapons capability. Twenty points of armor provide solid all-around protection. The Orc lacks jump jets, relying on its sixty-four kilometers per hour cruising speed for tactical maneuver. Every ProtoMek Star assigned to the Hell's Horses Alpha and Beta Galaxies fielded up to two Orcs, making it the most numerous ProtoMek type in the Clan's frontline forces.

The Orc 3 takes an aggressive approach to maximizing close-range firepower, mounting five SRM tubes total: one in each arm and three in the torso. Each arm tube carries six rounds while the torso triple feeds from a three-round magazine. To mount this increased firepower, the Orc 3 sacrifices four points of armor, dropping to sixteen points of protection. This makes the variant noticeably easier to destroy but correspondingly more dangerous in the opening moments of an engagement, when a full salvo from a Point of Orc 3s can devastate light and medium targets. The variant is typically assigned to the most aggressive ProtoMek pilots who favor decisive initial strikes over sustained engagements.

The Orc 4 stands as a compromise between the long-range Orc 2 and the close-combat Orc 3. A three-tube SRM launcher in the torso provides meaningful close-range punch, while machine guns in each arm handle anti-infantry work with sustained fire capability from a shared twelve-round ammunition supply. This combination gives the Orc 4 the most versatile engagement profile of any variant, capable of engaging infantry with machine gun fire, light vehicles with SRM volleys, and providing suppressive fire at multiple range bands. Armor drops to sixteen points, matching the Orc 3. Ground speed remains at sixty-four kilometers per hour cruising.

The Procyon Quad fulfills the original quadruped concept that Coyote engineers first envisioned but could not realize. Produced by Clan Hell's Horses at the Csesztreg Industriplex Epsilon, this six-ton four-legged design mounts dual AP Gauss Rifles with thirty-two rounds of ammunition alongside an SRM-2 launcher with five rounds, all concentrated in the torso. The quad chassis provides sixty-four kilometers per hour cruising speed, matching lighter bipedal ProtoMeks while carrying thirty points of armor that can survive a Gauss rifle hit to the torso. The AP Gauss Rifles can savage infantry formations while the SRM launcher handles armored targets. The design suffers from technician unfamiliarity with the unique quad configuration, leading to greater maintenance downtime, and its larger cockpit has proved problematic for veteran ProtoMek pilots accustomed to tighter bipedal designs.

The Procyon 2 trades the arm-mounted ER Small Lasers and heat sinks for twin torso-mounted LRM-4 launchers sharing six volleys of ammunition, supplemented by four additional points of armor bringing total protection to twenty-four points. This variant transforms the Procyon from a close-range energy fighter into a dedicated fire support platform capable of engaging targets beyond five hundred meters. The dual LRM-4 configuration puts eight missiles per salvo on target, serious firepower for a five-ton design. However, the short ammunition supply and complete lack of backup weapons leave the Procyon 2 dangerously vulnerable once its magazines are empty.

The Procyon 4 mounts a Streak SRM-3 launcher in the torso with five guided salvos and a machine gun in the right arm with twenty rounds of ammunition. The Streak system ensures no missile is wasted, making this the most ammunition-efficient missile variant in the Procyon family. The machine gun provides sustained anti-infantry capability that complements the missile launcher's anti-armor punch. Twenty points of armor and sixty-four kilometers per hour cruising speed match the base configuration. Point Commander Kreig demonstrated this variant's potential by defeating a Snow Raven Mek and two Points of Elementals in a combined-arms Trial using his Procyon 4 alongside four other ProtoMeks and a pair of Donar VTOLs.

The only bipedal Procyon variant to employ jump jets, the Procyon 5 mounts five body-mounted jump jets providing one hundred fifty meters of leaping distance alongside a right-arm ER Small Laser and a torso-mounted SRM-2 with five rounds. This combination gives the Procyon 5 the highest tactical flexibility of any variant, capable of engaging at range with the laser, closing under jump power, and delivering SRM volleys at short range. Armor increases slightly to twenty-three points. The jump capability allows the Procyon 5 to exploit terrain features denied to other variants and execute flanking maneuvers that leverage the ProtoMek's small profile.

text.deployment: The base Roc mounts an ER Medium Laser in the torso alongside five body-mounted jump jets providing one hundred and fifty meters of jumping distance. This energy-only armament eliminates ammunition dependency entirely, allowing the Roc to operate indefinitely without resupply. The sixty-rated fusion engine delivers fifty-four kilometers per hour cruising speed. Thirty-one points of armor provide solid protection for the weight class. First produced at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress, the base Roc subsequently achieved the widest production distribution of any first-generation ProtoMek, with lines established at the Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on Dante, Csesztreg Industriplex Epsilon under Clan Wolf, and multiple other Homeworld facilities.

text.deployment: The Roc 2 replaces the ER Medium Laser with a Heavy Medium Laser, substantially increasing damage output at short range at the cost of reduced effective range and armor protection. Twenty-one points of armor represent a significant reduction from the base model, making the Roc 2 considerably more fragile. The jump jet configuration remains unchanged at five jets providing one hundred and fifty meters of jumping distance. The Heavy Medium Laser generates considerable heat for a ProtoMek-scale weapon, but its raw damage output makes a Point of Roc 2s extremely dangerous to any target caught at close range.

text.deployment: The Roc 3 trades the jump jets for a Medium Pulse Laser and significantly heavier armor at twenty-six points. The pulse laser improved accuracy partially compensates for the loss of positional flexibility that jump jets provide. Cruising speed remains at fifty-four kilometers per hour. This ground-bound variant is deployed in defensive positions where jump capability is less critical and the additional armor allows the Roc 3 to hold terrain under fire that would force a base model to withdraw. The design is most common in garrison forces tasked with fixed-position defense.

The Roc 4 mounts an ECM Suite alongside an AP Gauss Rifle, creating a unique electronic warfare platform within the ProtoMek weight class. The ECM disrupts enemy targeting systems and communications within its area of effect, degrading the combat effectiveness of opposing forces while protecting friendly units from guided munitions. The AP Gauss Rifle provides self-defense capability. Thirty-eight points of armor, the highest of any Roc variant, allow the design to survive in the contested space near enemy formations where the ECM Suite is most effective. Five jump jets maintain the chassis trademark mobility.

The Roc 5 pushes the chassis jump capability to seven jets providing two hundred and ten meters of jumping distance, the highest of any standard Roc variant. Armed with a Medium Chemical Laser, this variant trades the ER Medium Laser extended range for a weapon that generates no heat, allowing continuous firing without the thermal management concerns that limit energy weapon ProtoMeks. Thirty-one points of armor match the base model. The enhanced jump capability combined with sustained-fire weaponry makes the Roc 5 exceptionally effective in mountainous and urban terrain where vertical mobility is decisive.

The base Satyr mounts an ER Small Laser in the torso alongside a light active probe, the first electronic detection system fitted to a ProtoMek chassis. The laser provides reliable, ammunition-independent firepower while the probe extends the Satyr detection envelope, allowing it to locate hidden enemies at extended range. The forty-five-rated engine delivers seventy-six kilometers per hour cruising speed with no jump capability. Armor protection is minimal at twelve points. First produced at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress, the base Satyr entered wider production across the Homeworlds after multiple Clans seized Smoke Jaguar technology following the Clan Annihilation.

The Satyr 2 dramatically reimagines the design by adding seven jump jets that provide two hundred and ten meters of jumping distance, the highest of any standard Satyr variant. The ER Small Laser is replaced with a Micro Pulse Laser for improved close-range accuracy, and armor is significantly increased to twenty points, nearly doubling the base model protection. This variant sacrifices the light active probe, shifting the role from electronic reconnaissance to mobile strike operations. The jump capability allows the Satyr 2 to exploit vertical terrain that ground-bound units cannot reach, making it exceptionally difficult to corner or trap.

The Satyr 3 combines five jump jets providing one hundred and fifty meters of jumping distance with a Streak SRM-2 launcher, giving the design meaningful anti-armor capability for the first time. The Streak system ensures that missiles only fire when a solid lock is achieved, conserving the limited ammunition supply. Armor is slightly improved to thirteen points over the base model. This variant drops the light active probe in favor of the weapon and jump systems, representing a shift from pure reconnaissance toward a light striker role. The Satyr 3 is commonly deployed alongside base-model Satyrs, with the probe-equipped units identifying targets and the missile-armed variants engaging them.

The Satyr 4 replaces the light active probe with a Light TAG laser designator alongside an AP Gauss Rifle, converting the design from a reconnaissance platform into a dedicated target spotter for indirect fire assets. The Light TAG can guide artillery strikes and semi-guided munitions onto designated targets, making a Satyr 4 Point extraordinarily dangerous when paired with Arrow IV or LRM-equipped support units. The AP Gauss Rifle provides self-defense capability against battle armor and light vehicles. Armor protection matches the base model at twelve points. This variant sees heaviest use in Clans that maintain significant indirect fire capabilities in their toumans.

The experimental Satyr XP pushes the chassis to its absolute limits with nine jump jets providing an extraordinary two hundred and seventy meters of jumping distance, the longest of any ProtoMek ever fielded. Armed with only an SRM-2 launcher carrying ten rounds, the XP variant is nearly defenseless in sustained combat but possesses terrain mobility that no other ground unit can match. The oversized jump jet array required a smaller engine, reducing cruising speed to sixty-five kilometers per hour. Armor protection remains at twelve points. Developed under Clan Jade Falcon oversight, the Satyr XP was designed for extreme terrain infiltration missions where reaching otherwise inaccessible positions justified the severe combat trade-offs.

The base Siren mounts a pair of light machine guns in the torso, each fed from a shared two-hundred-round ammunition supply. This armament is effective only against unarmored infantry and light vehicles, reflecting the design pure reconnaissance role. The massive forty-five-rated fusion engine dominates the internal layout, leaving minimal space for armor protection at just twelve points total coverage. With no jump jets, the Siren relies entirely on its extraordinary ground speed to navigate terrain obstacles and evade pursuit. First produced at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress, the base Siren entered production at several additional Homeworld facilities following the dispersal of Smoke Jaguar ProtoMek technology after 3060.

The Siren 2 upgrades the dual light machine guns to standard Clan machine guns, providing a modest improvement in sustained damage output against infantry formations. Speed and armor remain identical to the base model at one hundred and eight kilometers per hour cruising with twelve points of protection. The heavier ammunition consumption of standard machine guns slightly reduces patrol endurance, but the improved stopping power was deemed worthwhile for garrison security operations where the Siren might need to suppress organized resistance rather than merely observe and report.
text.battleHistory:
The Siren emerged from the Smoke Jaguar ProtoMek program as the dedicated reconnaissance design, filling a critical gap in the original lineup between the light Harpy and the combat-oriented Satyr. Jaguar scientists recognized early that ProtoMek formations would need organic scouting capability, and the Siren was designed from the ground up to maximize speed at the expense of all other considerations. The oversized engine that gives the Siren its remarkable performance was considered an engineering extravagance by some, but the resulting speed proved invaluable during testing.

During the Battle of Huntress in 3060, Sirens were among the first ProtoMeks deployed against Task Force Serpent. Their extreme speed allowed them to serve as couriers and scouts in the chaotic jungle fighting, carrying messages between Jaguar positions when communications were disrupted by Inner Sphere electronic warfare. Several Siren Points also conducted harassment raids against Serpent supply lines, using their speed to strike and withdraw before the surprised Inner Sphere troops could organize a response.

After the Jaguar Annihilation, the Siren was acquired by multiple Clans alongside other ProtoMek designs. Clan Snow Raven showed particular interest in the Siren, valuing its reconnaissance capability for the naval-oriented Clan long-range patrol doctrine. Clan Coyote also produced significant numbers of Sirens, finding the design useful for rapid response garrison duty on their scattered Homeworld enclaves. The simplicity of the Siren chassis and its reliance on readily available light machine guns made it one of the easier ProtoMek designs to manufacture.

Variant development for the Siren has focused on alternative weapon fits and incremental speed adjustments. The Siren 2 replaces the light machine guns with standard machine guns for marginally better anti-infantry punch. The Siren 3 trades engine capacity for a pair of SRM-1 launchers, giving it limited anti-armor capability at the cost of reduced speed. The Siren 4 incorporates a myomer booster and ER Micro Laser, maintaining the high-speed profile while adding an ammunition-independent weapon. The Siren 5 mounts an AP Gauss Rifle, the most recent variant designed for anti-battle-armor operations.

The Siren remains in production across the Homeworld Clans, though its role has been partially supplanted by faster second-generation designs like the Cecerops. Yet, the Siren low manufacturing cost and proven reliability ensure continued demand, particularly among Clans that maintain large garrison forces across multiple worlds. The design is most commonly encountered in mixed reconnaissance Points paired with heavier ProtoMeks that provide the combat power the Siren itself lacks.

text.deployment: The Siren 3 makes the most radical departure from the base design philosophy, replacing the machine guns with a pair of SRM-1 launchers that give it genuine anti-armor punch for the first time. This comes at a significant cost: the engine is downsized to reduce cruising speed to eighty-six kilometers per hour, still fast by ProtoMek standards but a substantial reduction from the base model. Each launcher carries only five rounds, limiting the variant to brief engagements before ammunition is exhausted. The Siren 3 is typically deployed in mixed Points where its missile capability complements the machine guns of base-model Sirens.

text.deployment: The most recent Siren variant, the Siren 5 mounts a single AP Gauss Rifle, giving it effective capability against battle armor and light vehicles that previous variants could barely scratch. The engine is downsized to eighty-six kilometers per hour cruising speed to accommodate the weapon and its ammunition supply. Armor protection remains at twelve points. The AP Gauss Rifle limited ammunition supply of forty rounds restricts sustained engagements, but the weapon armor-piercing capability makes the Siren 5 a credible threat to the battle armor scouts it is likely to encounter during reconnaissance operations.

The Svartalfa 2 strips the Chemical Lasers, Streak launcher, and machine gun to mount dual LRM-15 launchers, one in the torso and one in the main gun position. Twenty salvos of ammunition provide exceptional fire endurance by missile-armed ProtoMek standards. This massive long-range firepower comes at a steep armor cost, dropping protection to thirty-seven points, less than many standard-weight ProtoMeks. The Svartalfa 2 is deployed as a dedicated indirect fire support platform, using its gliding capability to reposition between volleys and maintain distance from opponents. Ground speed remains limited to roughly ten kilometers per hour, making the gliding mode essential for survival when threatened at close range.

The Svartalfa 3 replaces the entire weapons suite of the base model with five Medium Chemical Lasers: three in the torso and one in each arm. A seventy-five-round chemical fuel supply provides sustained engagement capability. The larger engine increases ground speed to fifty-four kilometers per hour cruising in WiGE mode, making the Svartalfa 3 the fastest variant. Armor is reduced to thirty-nine points, significantly lighter than the base model but still substantial by ProtoMek standards. The all-chemical-laser configuration eliminates the Streak system's devastating close-range punch but provides more consistent damage output across multiple engagements without the binary hit-or-miss nature of guided missiles.

The base Triton mounts a Streak SRM-4 launcher in the main gun position with ten volleys of ammunition, backed by an ER Micro Laser in the torso for extended engagements. Four body-mounted jump jets provide one hundred twenty meters of leaping distance. The Streak system's guided missiles ensure maximum ammunition efficiency, making the base Triton the ideal companion for Seeker warriors conducting extended patrols far from supply lines. Thirty-eight points of armor provide excellent protection. Cruising speed of forty-three kilometers per hour is adequate when supplemented by jump capability. Produced at the Triton Assembly Yard on Roche under Clan Goliath Scorpion, the design was included in the Clan's Chi Galaxy and deployed alongside Seeker formations.

The most radical Triton variant, the Triton 3 strips the entire weapons suite for a single Heavy Medium Laser mounted in the main gun position. While this dramatically reduces the design's tactical flexibility, the Heavy Medium Laser delivers devastating armor-piercing damage that can threaten targets far above the Triton's weight class. Complete ammunition independence makes the variant ideal for the longest-duration independent operations. Armor increases to forty-one points, the heaviest of any Triton configuration, allowing the design to close to optimal laser range under fire. Four jump jets are retained. This configuration appeared just before the HPG blackout, and limited intelligence suggests it was used sparingly by the most skilled ProtoMek pilots.
